title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試録序
聖天子眷念關陝實
國家□□□地爰□□子少保左都
御史□□□總制諸軍而保障之總
八郡而廵撫之者則有左副都御
史□□分三邊而廵撫之者則
有右都御史余子俊右副都御史
===
朱英張鵬鎮守則有太監劉祥都
督白□□廵按則有監察御史王
毓強珍馬維茲大臣曁諸臺憲夙
夜祗□□謹咸求仰荅
上心□□□厲□又以□□風化之原茲
而不理非急先□□□有也乃協心作
興激昂而抑□□□而藩臬重臣右
punctuated:
陝西鄉試録序
聖天子眷念關陝實國家□□□地，爰□□子少保、左都御史□□□總制諸軍而保障之；總八郡而廵撫之者，則有左副都御史□□；分三邊而廵撫之者，則有右都御史余子俊、右副都御史朱英、張鵬；鎮守則有太監劉祥、都督白□□；廵按則有監察御史王毓、強珍、馬維。茲大臣曁諸臺憲，夙夜祗□□謹，咸求仰荅上心□□□厲□。又以□□風化之原，茲而不理，非急先□□□有也。乃協心作興，激昂而抑□□□，而藩臬重臣右
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

His Sacred Majesty, the Son of Heaven, bears in his solicitous thoughts that Guanzhong and Shaanxi are truly a [vital strategic?] region of the state. Therefore, he [commissioned?] the Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Censor-in-Chief [name illegible] to serve as Supreme Commander of the various armies and safeguard it. As for the one who exercises overall governance over the eight prefectures as Grand Coordinator, there is Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief [name illegible]; as for those who divide the three frontier zones as Grand Coordinators, there are Right Censor-in-Chief Yu Zijun 余子俊 and Right Assistant Censors-in-Chief Zhu Ying 朱英 and Zhang Peng 張鵬; as for those serving as Grand Defenders, there are Eunuch Director Liu Xiang 劉祥 and Commissioner-in-Chief Bai [name illegible]; and as for those serving as Regional Inspectors, there are Investigating Censors Wang Yu 王毓, Qiang Zhen 強珍, and Ma Wei 馬維. These great ministers, together with the various censorial officials, are day and night reverently [diligent and?] cautious, all seeking to look up and answer His Majesty's mind [and encourage/exert themselves?]. Furthermore, considering that [schools/education?] are the source of moral transformation, if this is not put in order, it would not be [attending to what is of urgent priority?]. Thus, with united hearts they have promoted and encouraged it, rousing the spirited and restraining [the unruly?], while the senior provincial administrative and judicial officials—Right…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
布政使宋有文□參政梁璟右參
政龐勝孫仁副□□玘任璽嚴憲
□□□參議李□□參議魯能張
琳僉□晃左鈺李進王繼劉讓
姚明亦悉力於外內襄臻盛美至
若□□約時其懲勸則提學副
使伍福寔專任之用是八郡之內
===
文風丕振猗歟盛哉維成化甲午
歲□□之期藩臬以試事白于
巡撫巡按既得請遂責選士于提
學□□提調乃具禮幣聘〔志良〕
□□□□邑□□鑑衡志良等被聘
戰兢惕息慮□□□兹重負讓至
再至三不果□□就聘八月朔胥
punctuated: 布政使宋有文，□參政梁璟，右參政龐勝、孫仁，副□□玘、任璽、嚴憲、□□，□參議李□，□參議魯能、張琳，僉□晃、左鈺、李進、王繼、劉讓、姚明，亦悉力於外，內襄臻盛美。至若□□約，時其懲勸，則提學副使伍福寔專任之。用是八郡之內，文風丕振，猗歟盛哉！維成化甲午，歲□□之期，藩臬以試事白于巡撫、巡按。既得請，遂責選士于提學，□□提調。乃具禮幣聘〔志良〕□□□□邑□□鑑衡。志良等被聘，戰兢惕息，慮□□□兹重負，讓至再至三，不果，□□就聘。八月朔，胥…
translation_en:
…Administration Commissioner Song Youwen 宋有文; [Left?] Administration Vice Commissioner Liang Jing 梁璟; Right Administration Vice Commissioners Pang Sheng 龐勝 and Sun Ren 孫仁; Surveillance Vice Commissioners [副使] [?] Qi □玘, Ren Xi 任璽, Yan Xian 嚴憲, and [?]; [Left?] Assistant Administration Commissioner Li [?] 李□; [Right?] Assistant Administration Commissioners Lu Neng 魯能 and Zhang Lin 張琳; and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners [僉事] [?] Huang □晃, Zuo Yu 左鈺, Li Jin 李進, Wang Ji 王繼, Liu Rang 劉讓, and Yao Ming 姚明 also exerted their utmost efforts in the provinces, assisting from within and without to achieve this flourishing excellence. As for [enforcing regulations?] and timely meting out punishments and encouragements, Education-intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wu Fu 伍福 was in fact exclusively entrusted with this responsibility. Because of this, throughout the eight prefectures, the literary culture was greatly revitalized—how magnificent indeed!

In the jiawu year of the Chenghua reign (1474), when the time for the triennial [provincial examination] arrived, the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions reported the examination affairs to the Grand Coordinator and the Regional Inspector. Having obtained approval, they tasked the Education Intendant with selecting the scholars, and [entrusted the] Proctor [with the arrangements?]. Thereupon, they prepared ceremonial gifts to invite [me], Zhi Liang 志良, [and other educational officials from various?] districts [to take charge of?] the evaluation and selection. Upon receiving the invitation, I, Zhi Liang, and the others trembled with awe and held our breath in anxiety, fearing [that we would be unequal to?] this heavy responsibility. We declined two or three times, without avail, and [ultimately had to?] accept the invitation. On the first day of the eighth month, we all…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
會□省郎於是□□執事之職入
郡抱藝之士蓋□□□□然來至矣越
□□□□入院□□□其事者則巡
按監□□□史王錦而提調監試則
左布政使干璠按察使王朝遠副
使胡□□右叅議崔忠也既鎖院
乃相與戒飭曰賢俊登庸茲惟
朝廷重典有所容心是負
===
朝廷也□用心亦負
朝廷也毋私毋怠庶副乃任既戒誓
已又□□□于神明遂命題辛卯試
□□□□□之丁□□試之合三試
之文而觀之華□□□麗則所造雖殊
如有戾乎道□□□否也於是遵
punctuated: 會□省郎。於是□□執事之職、入郡抱藝之士，蓋□□□□然來至矣。越□□，□□入院。□□□其事者，則巡按監□□□史王錦；而提調、監試，則左布政使干璠、按察使王朝遠、副使胡□□、右叅議崔忠也。既鎖院，乃相與戒飭曰：「賢俊登庸，茲惟朝廷重典。有所容心，是負朝廷也；□用心，亦負朝廷也。毋私毋怠，庶副乃任。」既戒誓已，又□□□于神明，遂命題：辛卯試之，□□□□□之，丁□□試之。合三試之文而觀之，華□□□麗，則所造雖殊，如有戾乎道□□□否也。於是遵
translation_en: …assembled at the provincial capital [?]. Thereupon the officials charged with examination duties and the scholars possessing literary skill from the prefectures [八郡 / 入郡?] all came flocking in [?]. After [several days], [the examiners and officials] entered the examination compound. Serving as [Supervising Official] in charge of the affair was the Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor Wang Jin 王錦; serving as Proctors and Surveillance Officials were the Left Administration Commissioner Yu Fan 干璠, the Surveillance Commissioner Wang Chaoyuan 王朝遠, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner Hu […], and the Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Cui Zhong 崔忠. Once the compound was locked, they admonished one another, saying: "The elevation and employment of worthy and talented men is a great institution of the Imperial Court. To harbor any partiality in one's heart is to betray the Imperial Court; to [fail to] apply one's heart is likewise to betray the Imperial Court. Be neither partial nor lax, so that you may live up to your charge." Having completed their admonitions and oaths, they also [offered prayers] to the gods and spirits, and thereupon set the examination questions: on the xinmao day they examined the candidates, on the [jiawu day they again examined] them, and on the ding[you] day [they again] examined them. Bringing together the essays from all three sessions and reviewing them, whether florid or [plain, refined] or ornate, although their attainments differed, none were retained if they ran counter to the Way [?]. Thereupon, in accordance with…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
制額録其尤深於〔者六十五人又〕
會萃其姓氏及〔一優等者以爲〕
録〔一〕〔卷□序中告〕〔多士曰〕
朝廷録
而已哉士之自是致身者亦非售
其文〔〕利祿也上以誠求下不
得不僞夫科目下以忠事上不能
===
不於科目焉進之故夫百餘年來
下〔〕〔〕上賴其忠上下交而世
道泰者罔用此道故今求賢之途
非一〔〕〔以〕科目爲重者豈無所
自〔〕〔〕爾多〔〕茲甄録於主司
父兄親族重之〔〕〔〕邦重之矣將
大對
punctuated: 制額，録其尤深於〔者六十五人。又〕會萃其姓氏及〔一優等者以爲〕録〔一〕〔卷，□序中告〕〔多士曰：〕「朝廷録……而已哉！士之自是致身者，亦非售其文〔〕利祿也。上以誠求下，不得不僞夫科目；下以忠事上，不能不於科目焉進之。故夫百餘年來，下〔〕〔〕，上賴其忠，上下交而世道泰者，罔用此道。故今求賢之途非一，〔〕〔以〕科目爲重者，豈無所自〔〕〔〕！爾多〔〕茲甄録於主司，父兄親族重之，〔〕〔〕邦重之矣。將大對
translation_en: … the imperial quota, and recorded sixty-five men who were especially profound in [their learning?]. Furthermore, [we] compiled their surnames and personal names along with [the essays of those ranked in the top grade to form] a record in one [scroll, and in the preface?] admonished the many scholars, saying: "[In] the Court's selection [of scholars through the examination system, is it merely a matter of literary composition?]! For scholars who advance their careers from this point, it is likewise not about peddling their essays [to seek] emoluments and profit. Because superiors seek subordinates with sincerity, they cannot but [rely on?] [?] the examination system; because subordinates serve superiors with loyalty, they cannot but advance themselves through the examination system. Therefore, for over a hundred years, subordinates [have offered their service?] and superiors have relied on their loyalty; that superiors and subordinates are in harmony and the Way of the world is at peace is [never not?] through the use of this Way. Thus today, although the avenues for seeking the worthy are not limited to one, that the examination system is regarded as the most important—how could this be without reason! Now that you many [scholars] have been selected and recorded by the examiners, your fathers, elder brothers, and kinsmen esteem you, and your [communities and] the state esteem you. Soon you will present your grand replies at …"

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天廷取重於國天□□可不知所自重
矣乎知所自重□偲可久業可大
□□□□終其□□□司之見録家
邦之□□庶無負焉不然斯汙矣
斯無取於國於天下矣於乎可不
敬哉□□戒哉故事録成有序用
書終始以引于端焉
河南開封府鈞州儒學學正侯志
良譔
punctuated:
天廷，取重於國、天□□可不知所自重矣乎？知所自重，□偲可久，業可大，□□□□終其□□，□司之見録、家邦之□□，庶無負焉。不然，斯汙矣，斯無取於國、於天下矣。於乎，可不敬哉！□□戒哉！故事，録成有序，用書終始，以引于端焉。
河南開封府鈞州儒學學正侯志良譔。
translation_en:
… at the imperial court and win the esteem of the state and all under Heaven [?]—how could you fail to know how to hold yourselves in esteem? If you know how to hold yourselves in esteem, [then your resolve (?)] can be enduring, your achievements can be great, and [… (?)] to the end of your [lives (?)], so that you may perhaps not disappoint the examiners who selected you or the [expectations (?)] of your families and your state. Otherwise, you will be sullied, and there will be nothing in you worthy of adoption by the state or by all under Heaven. Alas! How could you not be reverent? [How could you not (?)] be on your guard? By precedent, when the examination record is completed there is a preface; therefore I have written out the whole course of the affair from beginning to end to place at the head of the volume.

Composed by Hou Zhiliang 侯志良, Director of Studies of the Confucian School of Jun Subprefecture 鈞州 in Kaifeng Prefecture 開封府, Henan 河南.

"When a person's knowledge is sufficient to attain it, yet their humaneness is insufficient to keep it, even though they [attain] it, they will surely lose it. When a person's knowledge is sufficient to attain it and their humaneness is sufficient to keep it, if they do not preside over the people with dignity, then the people will not respect them. "Such being the nature of absolute sincerity, it becomes manifest [without being seen], produces change without motion, and accomplishes its ends without action. The Way of Heaven and Earth may be completely declared in a single sentence: as Things, they are without doubleness, and so their production of things is unfathomable. The Way of Heaven and Earth is broad, thick, [high], [bright], far-reaching, and long-enduring. Look now at Heaven: it is but this bright shining spot, yet in its boundlessness, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations are suspended in it, and the myriad things [are overspread] by it. Look now at the Earth: it is but a handful of soil, yet in its breadth and thickness, it [supports] Mount Hua without feeling its weight, contains the rivers and seas without letting them leak away, and carries the myriad things upon it. Look now at a mountain: it is but a [fistful] of stones, yet in its vastness, grass and trees grow upon it, [birds] and beasts dwell on it, and precious treasures are brought forth from it. Look now at water: it is but a spoonful of [liquid], yet in its unfathomable depths, giant sea turtles, alligators, flood-dragons, …"

君子來朝，何錫予之？雖無予之，路車乘馬。又何予之？玄衮及黼。厲沸檻泉，言采〻〔〕，來朝，言觀其旂。其旂淠淠，鸞聲嘒嘒，載驂載駟，君子所屆。赤芾在〻〔〕，邪幅不〻〔〕。彼交匪紓，天子所予。

translation_en:
On the third day, Wushen, the Grand Protector [arrived in the morning] at the Luo River and divined about the site. Having obtained a favorable divination, he laid out and planned the city. On the [third day], Gengxu, the Grand Protector led the [assembled] Yin people to prepare the ritual sites at the bend of the Luo River; on the [fifth] day, Jiayin, the ritual sites were completed.
 Assist me in governing the [people I have] received; I [the One Man] have obtained [peace?]; be cautious in this, and let nothing come between us. From [this day onward, if anyone] offers a single word of counsel, I shall look throughout the end only to men of accomplished virtue to govern the people I have received.

Classic of Poetry (Shijing):
The lords come to court; what shall be bestowed upon them? Though there is nothing grand to give them, there are state carriages and teams of four horses. What else shall be bestowed upon them? Dark-emblazoned robes with dragon and axe patterns. Bubble, bubble goes the spring; we gather [its cress. The lords] come to court; we gaze upon their banners. Their banners flutter; the harness bells chime softly; with teams of three and teams of four horses, the lords have arrived. Red knee-covers are on [their knees; leg-wrappings are] bound below. In their intercourse they are not remiss; such are those upon whom the Son of Heaven bestows his gifts.
All the officers of Zhou [?] are illustrious from generation to generation. [Are they] not illustrious? Their plans are reverent and careful.
Mats are spread and upper mats laid out; stools are presented by [attendants in] waiting. The host presents the cup, the guest returns it; thegoblets are washed…

實而言歟？《爲善隱》所載有關于五倫，如娶啞、娶瞽及嫁孤者誰歟？《孝真事實》所載有關於五倫，如忠孝、孝忠、廢□言善、□欽詩者誰歟？《五倫書》所載嘉三書專示于世，其與舜之愼徽、湯之言善而克盡五倫者又誰歟？三誥、擊□聖教同歟？異歟？爾諸士子欽諷聖訓非一日矣，其悉心以對。

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
衡劉向鄭玄之〻議論也何爲而非
正歟唐祀天地〔至於圜丘上辛祈〕
穀孟夏雩于南郊秋〔於明堂其後〕
有大〔明南郊之祀其所行之禮又〕
皆許〻宗王中立蕭嵩之所定議也
何謂而非宜歟六天五帝分祭合祭
之〔紛〻不一亦可得而折衷〕
歟諸士于皆達禮樂者願求至當之
===
說
問廉者〔大關也吏不廉則治道〕
數是不獨有以律其身抑亦大有關
於治〻也周禮天官冢宰以聽官府
之六〔弊群吏之治一曰廉善二曰〕
廉能三曰廉敬四曰廉正五曰廉法
六曰廉辨其義〔得聞歟三代而上〕
吏不稱廉至漢〔□下廉吏之名始著〕
punctuated:
衡、劉向、鄭玄之〻議論也，何爲而非正歟？唐祀天地〔至於圜丘，上辛祈〕穀，孟夏雩于南郊，秋〔於明堂，其後〕有大〔明南郊之祀，其所行之禮，又〕皆許〻宗、王中立、蕭嵩之所定議也，何謂而非宜歟？六天、五帝分祭、合祭之〔紛〻不一，亦可得而折衷〕歟？諸士于皆達禮樂者，願求至當之說。
問：廉者〔大關也。吏不廉則治道〕數，是不獨有以律其身，抑亦大有關於治〻也。《周禮》天官冢宰以聽官府之六〔弊群吏之治，一曰廉善，二曰〕廉能，三曰廉敬，四曰廉正，五曰廉法，六曰廉辨，其義〔得聞歟？三代而上〕，吏不稱廉，至漢〔□下廉吏之名始著〕…
translation_en:
…the discussions of [Kuang] Heng 匡衡, Liu Xiang 劉向, and Zheng Xuan 鄭玄 [?]; why then were they considered improper? In the Tang, sacrifices to Heaven and Earth [were performed at the Round Mound (Huanqiu), praying for] grain on the first xin day [of the first month], performing the rain sacrifice (yu) at the southern郊 (suburban altar) in the first month of summer, and in autumn [sacrificing in the Hall of Light (Mingtang); later] there were the great [sacrifices at the southern suburban altar [?], and the rites practiced] were all determined and deliberated upon by Xu [Jing]zong 許敬宗 [?], Wang Zhongli 王中立, and Xiao Song 蕭嵩; why were they said to be inappropriate? As for the [conflicting and varied views] on whether the Six Heavens and Five Emperors should be sacrificed to separately or jointly, [can we also arrive at a balanced judgment on them]? All you gentlemen [?] are well-versed in rites and music; I wish to seek the most fitting explanation.

Question: Integrity (lian) [is of great importance. If officials lack integrity, the Way of governance] deteriorates [?]; thus, it is not only a means to discipline oneself, but also bears greatly upon governance [?]. In the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), the Minister of State (zhongzai) in the Ministry of State (tianguan) hears the six [accountings (?) of the government offices to assess the governance of the various officials: the first is called] integrity and goodness (lianshan), the second integrity and competence (lianneng), the third integrity and reverence (lianjing), the fourth integrity and uprightness (lianzheng), the fifth integrity and lawfulness (lianfa), and the sixth integrity and discernment (lianbian). [May we hear] their meanings? [In the Three Dynasties and earlier], officials were not praised for integrity; it was only from the Han [and later (?) that the reputation of "officials of integrity" (lianli) first became prominent]…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
者何歟以廉吏□言有畏四知而暮
夜却金者有歛□衆而志愈烈者誰
歟平蜀東歸惟有圖□身平江南止
載圖□□日誰歟田園貧相惟富詩書
入蜀□官琴鶴自隨者誰歟愧市白
集清節可仰不持一硯高風可慕者
誰歟□□謂廉吏之名有三曰自
然曰□□曰勉強可指其人而言其
===
實歟共推
聖朝屢下廉□有自外職而登廊廟者
有自卑官而陞崇職者有廉者既舉貪
者自□致治之美頡頏古昔諸士子
進用□□景慕前哲將以何人為法
歟明言之無隱
問富國足兵莫要屯田歷代沿革不
一而皆有法制□焉古有所謂募民
punctuated:
者，何歟？以廉吏□言：有畏「四知」而暮夜却金者，有歛□衆而志愈烈者，誰歟？平蜀東歸，惟有圖□，身平江南，止載圖□□日，誰歟？田園貧相，惟富詩書；入蜀□官，琴鶴自隨者，誰歟？愧市白集，清節可仰；不持一硯，高風可慕者，誰歟？□□謂廉吏之名有三：曰自然、曰□□、曰勉強，可指其人而言其實歟？共推聖朝屢下廉□，有自外職而登廊廟者，有自卑官而陞崇職者。有廉者既舉，貪者自□，致治之美，頡頏古昔。諸士子進用□□，景慕前哲，將以何人為法歟？明言之無隱。

問：富國足兵，莫要屯田。歷代沿革不一，而皆有法制□焉。古有所謂募民
translation_en:
…why is that? Speaking of incorrupt officials [?]: Who was it that feared the "four who know" and refused gold in the dead of night, and who was it whose resolve grew only fiercer when collecting [?] the multitude? Who was it that, returning east after pacifying Shu, had only maps and books [?], and who, having personally pacified Jiangnan, loaded only maps and books [?]? Who was the impoverished minister without estates, rich only in poetry and books; and who was the official entering Shu, accompanied only by a zither and a crane? Who was it that felt ashamed to buy the Collected Works of Bai Juyi, whose pure integrity is worthy of admiration; and who did not take away a single inkstone, whose lofty character is worthy of emulation? Someone [?] has said that there are three grades of reputation among incorrupt officials: that which comes naturally, that which is [?], and that which is achieved through effort—can you point to the specific individuals and explain the reality of their cases? It is universally recognized that Our Sacred Dynasty has repeatedly issued decrees regarding incorrupt [?]: some have ascended to the high court from provincial posts, and some have been promoted to exalted offices from humble ranks. When the incorrupt are promoted, the greedy naturally [?], and the splendor of the resulting governance rivals that of antiquity. As you gentlemen await appointment and advancement [?], admiring the former worthies, whom will you take as your model? State it clearly and hide nothing.

Question: For enriching the state and supplying the military, nothing is more essential than state farms (tuntian). Their institutional evolution has varied across the dynasties, yet in every case there were regulations and systems [?] in place. In antiquity, there was the practice of recruiting commoners…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
階而有苗格㴱〻至于大原而玁狁
遁先王馭夷狄〻廻有自來矣自是
以還德威不立而夷〻之患始滋熾
焉試一隱之密通者與諸生講之
自夫厂室東遷戎逼諸夏列國諸侯
亦有能合師征討以尊周室者矣果
得歟〻否歟地拘靈夏國無藩
垣當〻將帥亦有能守邊備寨以匡
宋祚者矣果能終致其服否歟我
===
朝受
天明命德威並施因已稽顙呼韓接踵屠耆
矣迨〻〻蕞爾醜虜肆其蜂蠆擾攘我
邊境〻〻劉我人民致壓
聖慮恭行
天討
神謀
punctuated: 階，而有苗格；㴱〻至于大原，而玁狁遁。先王馭夷狄〻廻有自來矣。自是以還，德威不立，而夷〻之患始滋熾焉。試一隱之密通者，與諸生講之。自夫厂室東遷，戎逼諸夏，列國諸侯亦有能合師征討，以尊周室者矣，果得歟〻否歟？地拘靈夏，國無藩垣，當〻將帥亦有能守邊備寨，以匡宋祚者矣，果能終致其服否歟？我朝受天明命，德威並施，因已稽顙呼韓、接踵屠耆矣。迨〻〻蕞爾醜虜，肆其蜂蠆，擾攘我邊境，〻〻劉我人民，致壓聖慮，恭行天討，神謀
translation_en:
… the steps, and the Youmiao submitted; marching [?] as far as Taiyuan, and the Xianyun fled. The ways in which the former kings controlled the Yi and Di barbarians [?] indeed had their origins long ago. From that time onward, virtue and majesty were not established, and the scourge of the Yi and Di [?] barbarians began to grow increasingly rampant. Let us examine those instances that lie in close proximity [?] and discuss them with you students.

From the time the royal house of Zhou [?] moved east and the Rong barbarians pressed upon the Chinese states, among the feudal lords of the various states there were also those capable of uniting armies to launch punitive expeditions in order to honor the royal house of Zhou; did they truly achieve the proper way of [controlling them?] or not? When territory was hemmed in by Lingzhou and Xiazhou and the state lacked defensive barriers, among the generals and commanders of that time [?] there were also those capable of guarding the frontiers and preparing stockades in order to uphold the dynastic fortune of the Song; were they truly able to bring about their submission in the end or not?

Our Dynasty received the bright Mandate of Heaven and exercised both virtue and majesty, so that already [barbarian chiefs] bowed their heads to the ground like Huhanye and followed on one another's heels like the Tuqi kings. Coming down to recent times [?], the petty and vile caitiffs unleashed their scorpion- and wasp-like venom, throwing our frontiers into turmoil and slaughtering [?] our people, to the point of weighing upon the Sage's concern; reverently executing Heaven's punishment, the divine strategy…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
□□出自
淵衷宿將元臣布列邊以用能殲厥渠魁大
懋捷功狼藉餘孽逃而遠去矣此誠
萬萬世□平無疆之休也慮恐醜虜
變詐行懷覬覦叵測謀不可不豫也伊
欲息兵士之疲省轉輸之勞而坐使
犬羊□犯邊庭其策何長萬一
肆傳效尤前日兵威不可不用也伊
欲奮鷹揚之勇遏亂略之始使射獵
===
不得□土其術何在昔周宣王
得備邊之策其後變也乃出於不備
之方□武帝通西域斷匈奴右臂而
單于□以所置之郡而入備邊之策
益亦難矣諸士子生□于斯籌之稔
矣幸悉告我將□而獻之于
punctuated: □□出自淵衷，宿將元臣布列邊以，用能殲厥渠魁，大懋捷功，狼藉餘孽逃而遠去矣，此誠萬萬世□平無疆之休也。慮恐醜虜變詐，行懷覬覦，叵測謀不可不豫也。伊欲息兵士之疲，省轉輸之勞，而坐使犬羊□犯邊庭，其策何長？萬一肆傳效尤前日，兵威不可不用也。伊欲奮鷹揚之勇，遏亂略之始，使射獵不得□土，其術何在？昔周宣王得備邊之策，其後變也，乃出於不備之方；□武帝通西域，斷匈奴右臂，而單于□以所置之郡而入，備邊之策益亦難矣。諸士子生□于斯，籌之稔矣，幸悉告我，將□而獻之于…
translation_en: …[and secret counsels?] issued from the depths of His Imperial Mind, while veteran generals and chief ministers were arrayed along the frontiers [?]; thus we were able to annihilate their chieftains and achieve great and glorious victories, so that the scattered remnants fled far away. This is truly a boundless blessing of [lasting] peace for ten thousand generations! Yet should we worry that the vile caitiffs, in their deceitful mutability, might come to harbor covetous designs, unfathomable plots must be guarded against in advance. If we wish to relieve the exhaustion of our soldiers and reduce the toil of transport and supply, while sitting calmly and causing those dogs and sheep [never] to violate our frontier courts, what policy would be best? Should they by any chance recklessly imitate [?] the offenses of former days, military might must be employed. If we wish to rouse hawk-like valor, check rebellious raids at their very inception, and keep those hunting [nomads] from [encroaching upon our] territory, wherein lies the method? In antiquity, King Xuan of Zhou (Zhou Xuanwang 周宣王) possessed a policy for frontier defense, yet when later upheavals occurred, they arose from quarters against which he had not prepared; Emperor Wu of [Han] ([Han] Wudi 漢武帝) opened communications with the Western Regions (Xiyu 西域) to sever the right arm of the Xiongnu 匈奴, yet the Chanyu 單于 [nonetheless] invaded through the very commanderies that had been established. Thus, devising policies for frontier defense is difficult indeed! You gentlemen, born and [raised] in this region, have pondered these matters thoroughly. Pray tell me all, so that I may [select] and present them to [the Court]…

知及之仁不能守之雖得之必失之知及之仁
能守之不莊以涖之則民不敬知及之仁能
守之莊以涖之動之不以禮未善也

聖人論人之爲學也 進其所已至而勉其所未至焉
蓋人之爲學不可以不勉也苟不能隨其所已至而
勉 其未至又豈爲學 哉思昔聖人之意若曰
有人才 此本心 然無微不燭此知 足以知此理也
知 足以知此理是學之已至矣使其一爲私意所蔽
物欲所累則仁不能守之仁不能守之是學之未至
也必隨得而隨失豈能有諸 乎知既及矣方寸之
間又能不爲私欲所間此 守此理也仁能守此
punctuated:
四書義

「知及之，仁不能守之；雖得之，必失之。知及之，仁能守之，不莊以涖之，則民不敬。知及之，仁能守之，莊以涖之，動之不以禮，未善也。」

孔昭

同考試官教諭李批：〔此題本論為學，場中作者皆無定見，終以學之已至、未至講貫成文，宜錄為學者式。〕

聖人論人之爲學也，進其所已至，而勉其所未至焉。蓋人之爲學，不可以不勉也。苟不能隨其所已至而勉其未至，又豈爲學哉？思昔聖人之意若曰：有人才此，本心然，無微不燭，此知足以知此理也。知足以知此理，是學之已至矣。使其一爲私意所蔽、物欲所累，則仁不能守之。仁不能守之，是學之未至也，必隨得而隨失，豈能有諸乎？知既及矣，方寸之間，又能不爲私欲所間，此守此理也。仁能守此

"When one's knowledge is sufficient to attain it, yet one's humaneness is insufficient to preserve it, even if one gains it, one will surely lose it. When one's knowledge is sufficient to attain it and one's humaneness is sufficient to preserve it, if one does not preside over them with dignity, the common people will not be reverent. When one's knowledge is sufficient to attain it, one's humaneness is sufficient to preserve it, and one presides over them with dignity, yet one moves them not in accordance with ritual propriety, it is still not perfected."

By Kong Zhao 孔昭

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zeng 曾 comments: [Most candidates failed to grasp the true meaning of this quotation; only this essay has succeeded.]
Associate Examiner and Instructor Li 李 comments: [This passage fundamentally discusses self-cultivation and learning. None of the candidates in the examination compound held a firm view of it, whereas this author thoroughly explicates the passage from start to finish in terms of what learning has already reached and what it has not yet reached. It should be recorded as a model for scholars.]
Examiner and Instructor You 游 comments: [Able to thoroughly integrate the commentary into a coherent essay; worthy of selection.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Hou 侯 comments: [Clear and concise; commendable.]

When the Sage discussed a person's pursuit of learning, he commended what one had already reached while urging one onward toward what one had not yet reached. Indeed, in pursuing learning, a person cannot fail to exert himself. If one is unable to follow up on what one has already reached by striving toward what one has not yet reached, how could that be called learning [missing characters in transcription]? Reflecting on the Sage's meaning in the past, it is as if he said: Suppose there is a person here [?] whose original mind is so [bright] that there is no subtlety it does not illuminate—this means his knowledge is sufficient to know this principle. That his knowledge is sufficient to know this principle marks what his learning has already reached. Yet if he allows himself once to be obscured by selfish intentions and entangled by material desires, then his humaneness cannot preserve it. That his humaneness cannot preserve it marks what his learning has not yet reached; what is gained will inevitably be immediately lost—how could he truly possess it within himself [?]? Now, when his knowledge has already attained it, and within his heart-mind he is further able to remain unseparated from it by selfish desires, then [his humaneness is sufficient to] preserve this principle. When his humaneness is able to preserve this…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
理是學之已至矣使其臨尸之際衣冠不正視瞻不
尊則不莊以涖之不莊以涖是學之未至也則民
慢易寧有畏敬之心乎知既及矣仁能守矣其臨民
也有威而可畏有義而可象又莊以涖之也莊以涖
之是學之已至矣也其鼓舞斯民也不以義理之節
文以斯民也不以義理當然而動之不以禮也
動之不以禮亦學之未至也又豈盡善之道哉然
學之已至則義理大學之未至可不致其勉乎
大抵知及仁守學至於仁則善有諸己而大本立矣
===
涖之不莊動之不以禮乃其氣稟學問之小疵亦非
盡善之道也言之以示人始則使知德之
全而責之備終則使知德愈全而責愈備不可以小
節之也學者勉諸
此者不而章不動而變無為而成天地之
道一言而盡也其為物不貳則其生物不
測天地之道博也厚也高也明也悠也久也
今夫天斯昭昭之多其無窮也日月星辰
繫焉萬物覆焉今夫地一撮土之多及其廣
punctuated:
理，是學之已至矣。使其臨尸之際，衣冠不正，視瞻不尊，則不莊以涖之。不莊以涖，是學之未至也，則民慢易，寧有畏敬之心乎？知既及矣，仁能守矣，其臨民也，有威而可畏，有義而可象，又莊以涖之也。莊以涖之，是學之已至矣。也其鼓舞斯民也，不以義理之節文，以斯民也，不以義理當然，而動之不以禮也。動之不以禮，亦學之未至也，又豈盡善之道哉？然學之已至，則義理大；學之未至，可不致其勉乎？大抵知及仁守，學至於仁，則善有諸己而大本立矣。涖之不莊，動之不以禮，乃其氣稟學問之小疵，亦非盡善之道也。言之以示人，始則使知德之全而責之備，終則使知德愈全而責愈備，不可以小節之也。學者勉諸！

此者，不而章，不動而變，無為而成。天地之道，一言而盡也。其為物不貳，則其生物不測。天地之道，博也，厚也，高也，明也，悠也，久也。今夫天，斯昭昭之多，其無窮也，日月星辰繫焉，萬物覆焉。今夫地，一撮土之多，及其廣…
translation_en:
…this principle, this shows that one's learning has already reached this point. Yet suppose that when overseeing the people [reading 民 for 尸], one's robes and cap are not proper and one's gaze is not dignified, then one does not preside over them with gravity. Not presiding over them with gravity shows where one's learning has not yet reached; the people will then be disrespectful and negligent—how could they have a heart of awe and reverence? When one's knowledge has attained it and one's benevolence can preserve it, and in overseeing the people one has majesty that inspires awe and deportment [reading 儀 for 義] that serves as a model, then one also presides over them with gravity. Presiding over them with gravity shows that one's learning has already reached this point. Yet suppose [?] that in rousing and inspiring these people, one does not do so through the refinements and regulations of moral principle, and in governing [?] these people, one does not do so through what is right according to moral principle—this is moving them not in accordance with ritual propriety. Moving them not in accordance with ritual propriety also shows where one's learning has not yet reached; how could this be the Way of complete perfection? Thus, where learning has already reached, moral principle is great [?]; where learning has not yet reached, how can one not exert oneself to strive for it? In general, when knowledge attains it and benevolence preserves it, and learning reaches the level of benevolence, then goodness is possessed within oneself and the great foundation is established. Failing to preside with gravity and failing to move them in accordance with ritual propriety are minor flaws in one's physical endowment and learning, yet they too fall short of the Way of complete perfection. [Confucius] spoke of this to instruct others: at first, to make them understand the completeness of virtue and require thoroughness of them; in the end, to make them understand that the more complete the virtue, the more thorough the requirement, and that one must not [neglect it] as a minor detail. Let scholars exert themselves in this!

Such being the case [from Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), ch. 26], without [displaying] it becomes manifest, without moving it produces changes, and without effort it accomplishes its ends. The Way of Heaven and Earth may be summed up in a single phrase: because as things they are without duplicity, their generation of things is unfathomable. The Way of Heaven and Earth is broad, thick, high, bright, far-reaching, and enduring. Look at the sky now: it is but this bright shining spot, yet in its boundlessness, the sun, moon, stars, and constellations are suspended in it, and the myriad things are sheltered beneath it. Look at the earth now: it is but a handful of soil, yet in its breadth…

今夫山一卷石之多及其廣大草木生之禽

…and depth, it supports Mount Hua without feeling its weight, contains the rivers and seas without letting them leak away, and all things are supported by it. The mountain now before us is only a handful of stones; yet in its vast expanse, grass and trees grow upon it, birds and beasts dwell on it, and precious treasures are discovered within it. The water now before us is only a dipperful of liquid; yet in its unfathomable depths, giant sea turtles, alligators, scaly dragons, fishes, and soft-shelled turtles are produced in it, and goods and wealth abound in it. The Book of Odes (Shijing) says, 'The ordinances of Heaven, how profound and unceasing!' That is to say, this is whereby Heaven is Heaven. 'Oh, how illustrious was the purity of King Wen's virtue!' That is to say, this is whereby King Wen was titled 'the Cultured' (Wen): pure, and likewise unceasing."

Examiner and Instructor You 游 comments: 〔This passage from the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) is a long topic and difficult to encompass as a whole. This essay analyzes it clearly and explains it thoroughly and aptly; it is a masterpiece.〕

When the Doctrine of the Mean discusses the efficacious function of the sage's utmost sincerity, it first illustrates it by reference to Heaven and Earth, and then further illustrates it by interpreting the words of the Book of Odes. Now, the virtue of the sage is of utmost sincerity and unceasing; therefore, his breadth and depth are able to match the breadth and depth of Earth, his loftiness and brilliance are able to match the loftiness and brilliance of Heaven, and the [enduring nature of] his breadth and depth…

text:
所之悠久又有以配乎天地之無疆焉惟聖人至誠
有如此者故以配乎天地而□之其功用也不待見
而自然章著不待動而自然變化以配天地無疆而
言之其功用也不見不動而無為也變也自然成化焉
聖人功用配乎天地如此不即天□以明之果何以
見□是故天地之道可一言而盡不過曰誠而已
其為物也誠一不貳故其生物之多有莫知其所以
然也天地之□□也故博厚極其博厚高明極
其高明而博厚高明又極其悠久也今夫天地以其
===
一處而言昭昭□□亦天也撮土之多亦地也及其無
窮則日月以□□萬物於是乎覆焉及其廣厚
華嶽載之而不重河海振之而不洩□□物於是乎載焉
今□水以其一處而言□之多□山也勺水之多
亦□也及其廣□□草木以生禽獸□石而寶藏見於
是乎興焉□其不測黿鼉蛟龍□之所生魚鼈之所息而
□□財又於是乎殖焉夫天地之道不貳不息而能生物
□□此固足以見聖人之至誠□不引詩而釋之又何
以明天地聖人同一至誠無息□□□□□□□□□大
punctuated: 所之悠久，又有以配乎天地之無疆焉。惟聖人至誠有如此者，故以配乎天地而□之，其功用也不待見而自然章著，不待動而自然變化；以配天地無疆而言之，其功用也不見不動而無為也，變也自然成化焉。聖人功用配乎天地如此，不即天□以明之，果何以見□？是故天地之道，可一言而盡，不過曰誠而已。其為物也，誠一不貳，故其生物之多，有莫知其所以然也。天地之□□也，故博厚極其博厚，高明極其高明，而博厚、高明又極其悠久也。今夫天地，以其一處而言，昭昭□□亦天也，撮土之多亦地也；及其無窮，則日月以□□，萬物於是乎覆焉；及其廣厚，華嶽載之而不重，河海振之而不洩，□□物於是乎載焉。今□水，以其一處而言，□之多□山也，勺水之多亦□也；及其廣□□，草木以生，禽獸□石，而寶藏見於是乎興焉；□其不測，黿鼉蛟龍□之所生，魚鼈之所息，而□□財又於是乎殖焉。夫天地之道，不貳不息，而能生物□□，此固足以見聖人之至誠；□不引詩而釋之，又何以明天地聖人同一至誠無息□□□□□□□□□大
translation_en:
…and its enduring nature matches the boundlessness of Heaven and Earth. Only because the sage possesses such utmost sincerity can one speak of [?] his matching Heaven and Earth: his functional efficacy becomes naturally manifest without waiting to be displayed, and naturally transforms without waiting to move; and speaking in terms of his matching the boundlessness of Heaven and Earth, his functional efficacy acts without display and without movement—that is, without deliberate action—and through transformation naturally brings about completion. Since the sage's functional efficacy matches Heaven and Earth like this, if one did not turn to Heaven and Earth [?] to elucidate it, how indeed could it be seen [?]?

Therefore, the Way of Heaven and Earth may be summed up in a single word: it is nothing more than sincerity. As entities, they are of a single, undivided sincerity, and thus their production of things is so abundant that none can fathom how it comes to be so. Because Heaven and Earth [?], their breadth and thickness reach the utmost of breadth and thickness, their height and brightness reach the utmost of height and brightness, and their breadth, thickness, height, and brightness furthermore reach the utmost of endurance. Now, as for Heaven and Earth, if we speak of them in terms of a single spot, a small gleaming patch of light [?] is also Heaven, and a mere handful of soil is also Earth. Yet when they reach their inexhaustible extent, the sun, moon, and stars are suspended there [?], and the myriad things are sheltered beneath them; when they reach their full breadth and thickness, they bear up Mount Hua without feeling its weight, contain the rivers and seas without letting them leak away, and the myriad [?] things are supported upon them. Now as for mountains [?] and waters, if we speak of them in terms of a single spot, a fistful [?] of stones is also [?] a mountain, and a dipperful of water is also water [?]. Yet when they reach their full breadth and greatness [?], grasses and trees grow upon them, birds and beasts dwell upon them [?], and stores of precious minerals are brought forth and rise up from them; and when they reach [?] their unfathomable depths, giant turtles, alligators, scaly dragons, and dragons are born [?] there, fish and soft-shelled turtles breed there, and wealth and goods [?] are multiplied therein.

Now, that the Way of Heaven and Earth is undivided and unceasing, and thus able to produce things [?], is certainly sufficient to show the utmost sincerity of the sage; yet [?] if one did not quote the Book of Odes (Shijing) and explicate it, how else could one make clear that Heaven, Earth, and the sage all share the same unceasing utmost sincerity [?] … great…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
維天之命於穆不已蓋謂天之所以為天以此誠也
於乎不顯文王之德之純蓋謂文王之所以為文
亦此誠也然天道不已文王純於天道亦不已是則
文王之純卽天之於穆不已而同一機天之不已與
文王之純無二卽文王亦天也文王卽天也豈可以
二之哉抑考此章言至誠無息之功用也自至誠無息以至無
為而成是言聖人至誠無息之功用也自天地之道
可一言而盡至天地以明至誠無息之功用
乎終篇引詩而終之又以明至誠無息之意焉天地
===
也聖人也一而二二而一者也夫何間然之有
易義
六四外比之貞吉象曰外比於賢以從上也九
五顯比王用三驅失前禽邑人不誡吉象曰
顯比之吉位正中也舍逆取順失前禽也邑
人不誡上使中也
同考試官訓導朱
〔批此題場中作者多以君臣剛柔為說惟此篇主〕
〔以比而得公道是之取爾〕
趙道
punctuated:
「維天之命，於穆不已。」蓋謂天之所以為天，以此誠也。「於乎不顯，文王之德之純。」蓋謂文王之所以為文，亦此誠也。然天道不已，文王純於天道亦不已，是則文王之純卽天之於穆不已而同一機，天之不已與文王之純無二，卽文王亦天也，文王卽天也，豈可以二之哉？抑考此章言至誠無息之功用也。自「至誠無息」以至「無為而成」，是言聖人至誠無息之功用也；自「天地之道，可一言而盡」至「天地」，以明至誠無息之功用乎？終篇引《詩》而終之，又以明至誠無息之意焉。天地也，聖人也，一而二、二而一者也，夫何間然之有？

《易》義

「六四，外比之，貞吉。《象》曰：外比於賢，以從上也。九五，顯比，王用三驅，失前禽，邑人不誡，吉。《象》曰：顯比之吉，位正中也；舍逆取順，失前禽也；邑人不誡，上使中也。」

同考試官訓導朱〔批：此題場中作者多以君臣剛柔為說，惟此篇主以比而得公道，是之取爾。〕
趙道
translation_en:
…“The ordinance of Heaven, how profound and unceasing it is!” This means that that whereby Heaven is Heaven is through this sincerity. “Ah! Is it not illustrious, the purity of King Wen’s virtue?” This means that that whereby King Wen was culturally accomplished (Wen) is also this sincerity. Thus the Way of Heaven is unceasing, and King Wen’s purity in the Way of Heaven is likewise unceasing. Therefore, the purity of King Wen is none other than the profound unceasingness of Heaven, sharing the exact same vital mechanism; the unceasingness of Heaven and the purity of King Wen are not two—meaning King Wen is also Heaven, and King Wen is one with Heaven. How could one treat them as two? Moreover, let us examine how this chapter speaks of the efficacy and function of utmost sincerity without cessation. From “utmost sincerity is ceaseless” down to “accomplishes without action,” it speaks of the efficacy and function of the sage’s utmost sincerity without cessation; from “the Way of Heaven and Earth may be completely declared in one sentence” down to “Heaven and Earth” [?], is it not to elucidate the efficacy and function of utmost sincerity without cessation? At the end of the passage, it quotes the Book of Odes (Shi) to conclude it, further illuminating the meaning of utmost sincerity without cessation. Heaven and Earth, and the sage, are one and yet two, two and yet one. What gap could there possibly be between them?

Expositions on the Classic of Changes (Yi)

“Six in the fourth place: Externally cleaving to him;贞 (persevering in rectitude) brings good fortune. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: ‘Externally cleaving to the worthy, in order to follow the one above.’ Nine in the fifth place: Illustrious cleaving (alliance). The king uses drivers on three sides only, and loses the game that runs off in front. The people of his towns do not warn one another; good fortune. The Commentary on the Images says: ‘The good fortune of illustrious cleaving comes from his position being correct and central. Letting go those that go against him and taking those that come to him—thus he loses the game in front. That the people of his towns do not warn one another is because the ruler above causes them to keep the mean.’”

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor (xundao) Zhu [Comment: Among the candidates in the examination hall writing on this topic, most framed their arguments around the ruler and minister, the firm and the yielding; only this essay focuses on attaining the Way of impartiality through alliance, and for this reason it was selected.]
By Zhao Dao.

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭游　批得本義之旨可嘉
考試官學正侯　批此篇說出上下相比以公正之道文
理平順可觀
下之比上衆其所之比下一於公此此爻象所以各
著其占而申其　也蓋比之道固　　丁正而尤貴乎
公　之四五如此爻象　人得了各著其占而申
其義以示人哉旦夫比之爲卦以親輔爲義爻至六
四以陰居陰　　初六而今也外惟九五陽明
是比蓋以陰從陽比得其正何有不吉乎以柔處柔
===
不近比於六三　也上惟九五中正是輔蓋以下
輔上輔得　　吉乎占者如是則正而吉矣
爻易之旨如此象復申之曰六四　以外比於賢者
由　有剛中之德賢　上而然耳惟其在上是
以　之者非阿　也下之比上乃　之宜爲從之者
非曲從也　之從上乃理之一焉夫下之比上如此
而上之比下何如爻至九五一陽居尊剛健中正卦
之群陰皆來比己顯其比民道而無私公其比民
之道而無蔽如天子不合　一　之網來者撫之
punctuated:
考試官教諭游，批：得《本義》之旨，可嘉。
考試官學正侯，批：此篇說出上下相比以公正之道，文理平順，可觀。
下之比上，衆其所；之比下，一於公。此此爻象所以各著其占而申其　也。蓋比之道，固　　丁正，而尤貴乎公。　之四、五如此，爻象　人得了各著其占而申其義以示人哉？旦夫《比》之爲卦，以親輔爲義。爻至六四，以陰居陰，　　初六，而今也外惟九五陽明是比，蓋以陰從陽，比得其正，何有不吉乎？以柔處柔，不近比於六三，　也上惟九五中正是輔，蓋以下輔上，輔得　　吉乎？占者如是，則正而吉矣。爻易之旨如此，《象》復申之曰：六四　以外比於賢者，由　有剛中之德，賢　上而然耳。惟其在上，是以　之者非阿　也，下之比上，乃　之宜爲；從之者非曲從也，　之從上，乃理之一焉。夫下之比上如此，而上之比下何如？爻至九五，一陽居尊，剛健中正，卦之群陰皆來比己，顯其比民道而無私，公其比民之道而無蔽。如天子不合　，一　之網，來者撫之…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor You, comment: "Grasps the purport of the Original Meaning (Benyi); commendable."
Examiner and Director of Studies Hou, comment: "This essay brings out the Way by which superiors and inferiors form close alliance through impartiality and rectitude; the reasoning and style are smooth and well worth reading."

When inferiors ally with superiors, they rectify [?] their place; when [superiors] ally with inferiors, they are unified in impartiality. This is why the line statements and the Commentary on the Images (Xiang) of the Classic of Changes (Yi) each set forth their prognostications and elaborate on their [meaning]. For the Way of alliance (Bi) indeed [values] rectitude, and especially prizes impartiality. When the fourth and fifth lines of [Bi] are like this, how could the makers [?] of the line statements and Commentary on the Images not each set forth their prognostications and elaborate on their meaning in order to instruct people?

Now, the hexagram Bi (Alliance) takes intimate assistance as its meaning. When the lines reach the Six in the Fourth place, as a yin line occupying a yin position, [it does not respond inside to] the Six at the Beginning, and now on the outside it allies solely with the bright yang of the Nine in the Fifth place. Because yin follows yang, its alliance attains rectitude—how could it not be auspicious? As a yielding line abiding in a yielding position, it does not closely ally with the Six in the Third place, [and now] above it assists solely the central and correct Nine in the Fifth place. Because the inferior assists the superior, its assistance attains [what is right—how could it not be] auspicious? If the diviner is like this, then by being correct there will be good fortune.

Such is the purport of the line statement in the Changes. The Commentary on the Images again elaborates on it, saying: The reason why the Six in the Fourth place allies externally with a worthy is because [the Nine in the Fifth] possesses the virtue of strength and centrality, a worthy [occupying the position] above, and thus it is so. Only because he is above, therefore allying with him is not flattering [alliance]; for the inferior to ally with the superior is what is fitting by [duty]. Following him is not crooked compliance; for [the inferior] to follow the superior is the unity of principle.

Now, if the inferior's allying with the superior is like this, what of the superior's allying with the inferior? When the lines reach the Nine in the Fifth place, a single yang line occupies the honored position, strong, vigorous, central, and correct, and all the yin lines of the hexagram come to ally with him. He makes manifest his Way of allying with the people without selfishness, and makes impartial his Way of allying with the people without obscuration. Just as the Son of Heaven does not close [the surround on all sides, leaving open] three sides of the net: those that come he receives gently…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
□不拒去者舍之而不追是〔□〕王用三驅失前禽而
□人不誠之象蓋雖私屬亦上意不相警備以求
□得凡此皆吉之道占者如是明無不吉矣爻易之
□如此象復申之曰九五所以顯比而吉者由其得
□之正居上□之中而然耳謂□□曰失前禽者蓋
以□而去者舍之順□□者取之也謂之曰邑人
不誠者蓋由其在上之德使之而不偏也爻象聖人
互明其義□□矣抑考比之六爻皆以比五
爲主初六比之如先於比者故有他吉上六比之終
===
後於比者故有無首之凶二以應五而內比四以承
五而外比比〔□〕皆曰貞吉惟三不知比而反
應於上故有匪人之傷也不然何以謂九五曰以一
人〔□〕萬邦以四海而□□之□學易者觀之
擬之而後□議之而後動擬議以成其變化鳴
鶴在陰其子和之我有好爵吾與爾靡之子
曰君子居其室出其言善則千里之外應之
況其邇者乎居其室出其言不善則千里之
外違之況其邇者乎〔出乎身加乎民行發〕
punctuated:
□不拒，去者舍之而不追，是〔□〕「王用三驅，失前禽，而□人不誠」之象。蓋雖私屬，亦上意不相警備以求□得。凡此皆吉之道，占者如是，明無不吉矣。爻易之□如此，象復申之曰：九五所以顯比而吉者，由其得□之正，居上□之中而然耳。謂□□曰「失前禽」者，蓋以□而去者舍之，順□□者取之也；謂之曰「邑人不誠」者，蓋由其在上之德，使之而不偏也。爻象聖人互明其義□□矣。抑考比之六爻，皆以比五爲主。初六比之如，先於比者，故有他吉；上六比之終，後於比者，故有無首之凶；二以應五而內比，四以承五而外比，比〔□〕皆曰貞吉；惟三不知比，而反應於上，故有匪人之傷也。不然，何以謂九五曰以一人〔□〕萬邦，以四海而□□之□？學易者觀之。

「擬之而後□，議之而後動，擬議以成其變化。『鳴鶴在陰，其子和之。我有好爵，吾與爾靡之。』子曰：『君子居其室，出其言善，則千里之外應之，況其邇者乎？居其室，出其言不善，則千里之外違之，況其邇者乎？〔出乎身，加乎民；行發〕』」
translation_en:
…and does not reject [them], while letting go of those who leave without pursuing them. This is the image of [?]: "The king uses three-sided drives, losing the game in front, and the people of the towns do not need to be warned [誠 for 誡]." For even his private dependents [understand] the sovereign's intention and do not warn or guard against one another in order to seek mandatory [?] gains. All of these are the ways of good fortune; if the diviner acts thus, clearly there will be nothing that is not auspicious. Such is the [meaning] of the line in the Changes, and the Commentary on the Images (Xiang) further elaborates on it, saying: The reason Nine in the Fifth Place manifests alliance and has good fortune is simply because its position attains correctness and it dwells in the center of the upper trigram. What is meant by "losing the game in front" is that it lets go of those who turn away and leave, and takes in those who submit and come [?]; what is meant by "the people of the towns do not need to be warned" is that the virtue of the one above causes them to be centered and unbiased. Through the line statement and the Image commentary, the sages mutually illuminated its meaning [completely?]. Moreover, if we examine the six lines of the Bi (Alliance) hexagram, all take allying with the Fifth line as their lord. Six at the Beginning is at the start [如 for 始] of alliance, being first to ally, and thus has "unexpected good fortune." Six at the Top is at the end of alliance, being last to ally, and thus has the misfortune of "having no head." The Second line allies internally by corresponding with the Fifth, and the Fourth line allies externally by supporting the Fifth; in allying [with the Fifth?], both are called "correct and auspicious." Only the Third line does not know to ally [with the Fifth] and instead corresponds with the Top line, thus suffering the injury of "[allying with] the wrong people." Otherwise, why would it be said of Nine in the Fifth Place that as one man [he governs/allies with?] the myriad states, and with the four seas [looks up to one person?]? Let students of the Changes observe this.

"One forms a model of it and afterward [speaks]; one deliberates on it and afterward acts. Through modeling and deliberation, one brings about its transformations. 'A calling crane is in the shade; its young answers it. I have a fine goblet; I will share it with you.' The Master said: 'When the superior man dwells in his chamber and utters words that are good, those more than a thousand li away will respond to him—how much more so those who are near! When he dwells in his chamber and utters words that are not good, those more than a thousand li away will oppose him—how much more so those who are near! [Words] issue from one's person and affect the people; actions proceed…'"

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:

辱之主也言行君子所以動天地也可不
慎乎
閻仲宇

學易者歟
考試官教諭游　批明潔可錄
考試官□侯　批此作能發明擬議之例且行文
潔特表出之
===
大傳論人之言動以於易而妙其用必釋文辭以示
其例也蓋人
不法之於易又何以妙其用哉是聖人舉文辭而
釋之示其例也且夫易象有辭學易者將有言
動而不觀象玩辭擬之於易而後言乎易有變有占
易者將有為也可不觀變玩占議之於易而後動
言焉而擬之於易則淺深詳畧各當其理而易之
變化成於擬議之言矣動焉而議之於易則仕止久速
合適其時而易之變化成於擬議之動矣然人之言動
punctuated:
乎邇、見乎遠。言行，君子之樞機；樞機之發，榮辱之主也。言行，君子所以動天地也，可不慎乎？」
閻仲宇。
同考試官訓導朱　批：此作寸擬議之旨，其亦善於學《易》者歟！
考試官教諭游　批：明潔，可錄。
考試官□侯　批：此作能發明擬議之例，且行文潔，特表出之。
大傳論人之言動以於《易》而妙其用，必釋文辭以示其例也。蓋人……不法之於《易》，又何以妙其用哉？是聖人舉文辭而釋之，示其例也。且夫《易》象有辭，學《易》者將有言動，而不觀象玩辭，擬之於《易》而後言乎？《易》有變有占，《易》者將有為也，可不觀變玩占，議之於《易》而後動？言焉而擬之於《易》，則淺深詳畧各當其理，而《易》之變化成於擬議之言矣；動焉而議之於《易》，則仕止久速合適其時，而《易》之變化成於擬議之動矣。然人之言動，

"The lordly men come to court; what shall be bestowed upon them? Though there is nothing adequately to give them, there are state carriages and teams of four horses. What more is given to them? 春秋義
translation_en:
… [not one officer] alone, all are brilliantly illustrious, carrying forward their excellence from generation to generation and sharing in the blessings of the state. Not only did Heaven cause King Wen's collateral descendants to be feudal lords for a hundred generations, it also extended this to his ministers and officers, causing all the officers of our Zhou who hasten about on service and ward off insults—not one officer alone—to be radiantly glorious, cultivating their [virtue?] from generation to generation and sharing in the righteousness of the state. Finding his words insufficient, the poet speaks of it once more, saying: "As for the [officers?] of Zhou, is not their hereditary transmission illustrious? As for the ministers and sons of Zhou, is not their succession across generations glorious?" Those officers who drew the distant near and attended before and behind in our House of Zhou were indeed already diligent and reverent in their counsels and plans; and those who succeeded them from generation to generation, in their admirable plans [?], likewise all bent their bodies and exhausted their strength, not daring to [slacken?]. How great was their eminence from generation to generation! Those officers who hastened about on service and warded off insults in our House of Zhou were likewise already diligent and reverent in their counsels and plans; and those who succeeded to their virtue across the generations, with great counsels and far-reaching foresight, likewise all humbled themselves to join their strength, not daring to indulge in neglectful ease. How great too was the eminence of their hereditary transmission! Given the flourishing of King Wen's [virtue and the multitude of his officers?], that the eminence of their hereditary transmission should fittingly be such as this—if one said this was not due to Heaven's favor upon the Zhou, could it have been so? Moreover, if we consider King Cheng, endowed with a young and tender nature and presiding over an era of full accomplishment, he perhaps did not yet know the reasons for receiving the Mandate and the causes of obtaining [men?]. As the closest relative of the royal house, how could the Duke of Zhou not be deeply concerned for him? Therefore he composed this ode to admonish [him]; how earnest was his desire that the King should cultivate virtue and obtain worthy men so as to preserve the Mandate of Heaven! Alas! Passing through twenty [thirty] generations and lasting eight hundred years, that the ordained tenure of the Ji clan of Zhou ultimately surpassed its predicted span—was it not founded upon this?

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
堂堂之陣大伐于陘次于召陵之役直抵于方城進
□于陘按兵不動宣威討罪問以包茅之不貢伏
我執言而責以王祭之不共桓公之攘楚也為何如
是楚人震恐屈完惠來則認罪於行陣之前納款
門之下楚盟其義而求盟于召陵退召陵而以
楚人之服若是使桓不能明義於內是又
不知所重也桓也有見于此乃因王溺愛之私遂
首止之會之文是講世子之命駕寔臨尊
以非常之禮冊以尊戴之義大義一申大本遂定若
===
內若外而舉知世子之所當尊無小無大而咸知子
鄭之不可易之義也又何如吁楚人未服而
齊桓仗義以伐楚楚人既服而齊
盛一舉也雖然齊桓今之仗義以伐楚固可美
矣楚伐黃而不能恤敗徐而莫能救義
在哉今日之會首止以明之義可美矣其後屬
公於宰而致伐齊之役四子爭亂而子亂有戰其
義又安在哉一齊桓也何始之相反耶詩曰靡不
有初鮮克有終齊桓是已讀之不可不知
punctuated: 堂堂之陣，大伐于陘，次于召陵之役，直抵于方城。進□于陘，按兵不動，宣威討罪，問以包茅之不貢，伏我執言，而責以王祭之不共。桓公之攘楚也為何如！是楚人震恐，屈完惠來，則認罪於行陣之前，納款門之下。楚盟其義而求盟于召陵，退召陵而以。楚人之服若是，使桓不能明義於內，是又不知所重也。桓也有見于此，乃因王溺愛之私，遂首止之會之文。是講世子之命駕寔臨，尊以非常之禮，冊以尊戴之義。大義一申，大本遂定，若內若外而舉知世子之所當尊，無小無大而咸知子鄭之不可易。之義也又何如！吁！楚人未服，而齊桓仗義以伐楚；楚人既服，而齊盛一舉也。雖然，齊桓今之仗義以伐楚，固可美矣；楚伐黃而不能恤，敗徐而莫能救，義在哉？今日之會首止以明之義，可美矣；其後屬公於宰，而致伐齊之役，四子爭亂，而子亂有戰，其義又安在哉？一齊桓也，何始之相反耶？《詩》曰：「靡不有初，鮮克有終。」齊桓是已。讀之不可不知。
translation_en: …with an imposing battle array, launched a major punitive expedition to Xing, and in the campaign where he halted at Shaoling, pressed straight to Fangcheng. Advancing and halting [?] at Xing, he held his troops motionless, displaying his majesty to punish their crimes. He interrogated them over their failure to present the bundled coarse grass as tribute, making them submit to our righteous words, and rebuked them for leaving the royal sacrifices unsupplied. How grand was Duke Huan's repelling of Chu! Thus the men of Chu trembled in fear, and when Qu Wan graciously came, he admitted their guilt before the battle ranks and offered submission beneath the camp gates. Chu acknowledged [?] his righteousness and sought a covenant at Shaoling, after he had withdrawn to Shaoling [?]. With the men of Chu submitting like this, had Huan been unable to clarify righteousness within the realm, he would again have failed to know what was most important. Huan saw this clearly, and so, in response to the King's private partiality and doting affection, he consequently held the meeting at Shouzhi [?]. At this meeting [?], the Heir Apparent commanded his carriage and personally attended; Huan honored him with extraordinary ritual and confirmed [?] him with the principle of reverent allegiance. Once this great principle was proclaimed, the great foundation of the state was settled: both inside and outside the court, all knew that the Heir Apparent ought to be honored; great and small alike, all knew that Prince Zheng could not be displaced. How grand, too, was his clarifying [?] of righteousness! Alas! When the men of Chu had not yet submitted, Huan of Qi upheld righteousness to attack Chu; once the men of Chu had submitted, Huan of Qi [held the meeting at Shouzhi to clarify righteousness—truly] a flourishing double [?] achievement! Even so, Huan of Qi's upholding righteousness to attack Chu today is certainly praiseworthy; yet later, when Chu attacked Huang he could not relieve it, and when Chu defeated Xu he could not rescue it—where then was his righteousness? Today's meeting at Shouzhi to clarify righteousness is praiseworthy; yet afterward he entrusted Duke [Xiao] to the ruler of Song, bringing about the campaign to attack Qi, while his four sons contended in disorder and fought in civil war [?]—where then was his righteousness? It was the very same Huan of Qi; why were his beginning and his end so contrary to each other? The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "There is nobody who does not have a beginning, but few can have a good end." Such was Huan of Qi indeed. Those who read [the Spring and Autumn Annals] cannot fail to know this.

論

punctuated:
不敢委置於地焉，此「侍投則〔亦然也〕」。然射與投壺，禮必有勝負之分。彼常禮，〔主人〕行勝者之弟子酌酒於豐上，不勝者跪而飲之；若卑者得勝，則不敢徑當，前洗爵而請行觴也；客若不勝，則主人亦當洗爵而請，所以優賓也。至若角者，罰〔爵〕之兕觥也，因投射〔之〕勝，行兕觥之罰爵，〔而〕施於敵己者然也；今飲尊者及客，不敢用角，但當如常獻之爵焉。馬者，投壺之勝算也，〔立之〕一馬足成己之三馬，此行於同等宜也；今卑者雖得二馬，不敢取尊者之一馬以成己勝焉。吁！先王於射投之禮，孰有加於此哉？柳誼：射者，男子之〔事〕；射，禮之細也。故其容體比〔於禮〕，節奏比樂，志正體直，而後審固而〔中者同一〕所以觀〔其德〕馬。為非因人情而〔為〕之節文，又何足以為禮？□亂者著此以《少儀》之篇，無非〔使〕人知射投之中，又有尊卑之等、賓主之分，而敬讓之節不可以忝歟！

天子爲萬世之基
translation_en:
… dare not lay them down on the ground; this is what is meant by "when attending at pitch-pot, [one holds the arrows together] likewise."

Yet in the rituals of archery and pitch-pot, there must be a distinction between winner and loser. According to ordinary ritual, [when the host] carries out the penalty, a younger attendant of the winner pours wine upon the vessel-stand (feng), and the loser kneels and drinks it. If the junior wins, however, he does not dare let it be done directly, but steps forward to wash the goblet and request permission to present the cup. And if the guest fails to win, the host likewise must wash the goblet and make the request, as a way of showing special courtesy to the guest.

As for the "horn" (jiao), it is the rhinoceros-horn cup (sigong) used as a penalty [goblet]. Administering the penalty goblet of the rhinoceros-horn cup upon winning in pitch-pot or archery is practiced toward one's equals. Now, when giving a drink to a superior or a guest, one does not dare use the horn, but should only use a goblet as in an ordinary toast. As for the "horses" (ma), they are the tallies of victory in pitch-pot. Taking the opponent's [established] single tally to complete one's own three tallies is appropriate when practiced among equals. Now, even if the junior has obtained two tallies, he does not dare take the superior's single tally to complete his own victory.

Alas! In the rituals of archery and pitch-pot established by the former kings, what could surpass this? Or again [?], archery is the [affair] of a man, while pitch-pot [?] is a minor detail of ritual. Yet because in both one's deportment accords [with ritual] and one's rhythm accords with music—one's mind being upright and body straight before aiming steadily and [hitting the mark—they are the same in] serving as a means to observe [virtue] therein [?]. If this were not a matter of establishing regulated forms on the basis of human feelings, how could it suffice to constitute ritual? That the compiler [?] recorded this in the "Minor Rules of Demeanor" ("Shaoyi") chapter was simply to [make] people understand that even within archery and pitch-pot there are gradations of superior and inferior and distinctions between guest and host, and that the rules of reverence and deference must never be disgraced!

Discourse

"The Son of Heaven Lays the Foundation for Ten Thousand Generations"

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
李璽
考試官教諭游〔批此論垂萬世之基本諸禮樂深得本旨議論滔滔秋闈首〕
薦舍子其誰
考試官學正侯〔批文論精密措詞雄健傑作也擢冠多士孰曰〕
不
聖人有作而所以無窮之業必自一身始
焉蓋身也者作禮樂之本也惟一身之極建於
上故以之聞禮而禮備以之作樂而樂和統攝
人心者
天下者在是培植國本者在
是其規模蓋已綽綽乎有餘矣彼其工文章制
度者曰吾之禮可以爲萬世也然禮之末節耳
詞徇一時矣而遺之後世
奏者曰吾之樂可以垂萬世也然樂之粗迹耳
詞徇一時可矣而遺之後世則未焉然則天子
垂萬世之基者果何在
中和之極以基天下曰盡萬世之基意蓋如
punctuated:
李璽
考試官教諭游〔批：此論垂萬世之基，本諸禮樂，深得本旨，議論滔滔，秋闈首〕薦，舍子其誰？
考試官學正侯〔批：文論精密，措詞雄健，傑作也。擢冠多士，孰曰〕不！
聖人有作，而所以無窮之業，必自一身始焉。蓋身也者，作禮樂之本也。惟一身之極建於上，故以之聞禮而禮備，以之作樂而樂和。統攝人心者，天下者在是，培植國本者在是，其規模蓋已綽綽乎有餘矣。彼其工文章制度者曰：「吾之禮可以爲萬世也。」然禮之末節耳，詞徇一時矣，而遺之後世。奏者曰：「吾之樂可以垂萬世也。」然樂之粗迹耳，詞徇一時可矣，而遺之後世則未焉。然則天子垂萬世之基者果何在？中和之極以基天下，曰「盡萬世之基」，意蓋如
translation_en:
Li Xi 李璽

Examiner and Instructor You 游 [comment: This discourse on establishing a foundation for ten thousand generations roots it in rites and music, deeply grasping the essential meaning. Its argumentation flows torrentially. For the top] recommendation in the autumn Provincial Examination, if not you, then who?

Examiner and Director of Studies Hou 侯 [comment: The literary argument is precise and thorough, and the phrasing is vigorous and robust—a masterpiece! Selecting him to top the multitude of scholars, who would say] not [fitting]!

When a sage arises, that by which he [establishes] an endless enterprise must begin from his own person. For one's own person is the foundation for creating rites and music. Only when the supreme standard of one's own person is established on high can rites be made complete when one sets them forth [? 聞禮], and music be made harmonious when one creates it. That which unifies and governs human hearts, [that which orders?] the empire lies herein, and that which nurtures the foundation of the state lies herein; its grand scale is indeed already more than sufficient. Those who merely master outward literary forms and institutional regulations say: "My rites can serve for ten thousand generations." Yet those are merely the minor details of rites; they may suffice to accommodate a single era [?], [yet fail to] be handed down to later generations. Those who [master] musical performances [? 奏] say: "My music can be handed down for ten thousand generations." Yet those are merely the coarse traces of music; they may suffice to accommodate a single era, yet they cannot be handed down to later generations. If so, then wherein does the Son of Heaven's handing down a foundation for ten thousand generations truly lie? [In establishing] the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony in order to lay the foundation for the empire. When the text says "establishing [? 盡] a foundation for ten thousand generations," its meaning is likely like…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
此愚請得而詳其說天〔亦即人也既付之以莫〕
大之德又畀之以莫大〔之位豈徒私於聖人而尊〕
榮其身哉蓋將以爲天地立心爲生民立命爲萬
世開太平也聖人者出然天立極而父母斯民將
何以仰答上天付畀之意耶〔惟〕建中和之極以
帥禮作樂而已中和者〔吾身未發之禮樂禮樂者〕
吾身已發之中和也靜焉而無〔偏倚則中極其〕
中而大〔本〕以立也動焉而無少差謬則和
極其和而達道之所以行也大本以立則中之
===
極建矣達道以行則和之極建矣由是而帥禮
則大禮〔與〕天地同其節由是而作樂則大樂與
天地同其和制爲彝倫〔之〕叙〔立〕爲節秩秩乎其有
予也流爲德澤形爲〔歌〕頌雍雍乎其有章也于
以定民志於無爲之際而家〔家〕天下皆囿於吾
禮之中所謂至禮不讓而天下治者是已于以
和民心於不言之表而家國天下舉歸於吾樂
之內所謂至樂無聲〔而〕天下和者是已禮
一制而民志以定樂一〔奏〕而〔民〕心以和刑措不
punctuated: 此。愚請得而詳其說：天〔亦即人也，既付之以莫〕大之德，又畀之以莫大〔之位，豈徒私於聖人而尊〕榮其身哉？蓋將以爲天地立心，爲生民立命，爲萬世開太平也。聖人者出，然天立極而父母斯民，將何以仰答上天付畀之意耶？〔惟〕建中和之極，以帥禮作樂而已。中和者，〔吾身未發之禮樂；禮樂者，〕吾身已發之中和也。靜焉而無〔偏倚，則中極其〕中，而大〔本〕以立也；動焉而無少差謬，則和極其和，而達道之所以行也。大本以立，則中之極建矣；達道以行，則和之極建矣。由是而帥禮，則大禮〔與〕天地同其節；由是而作樂，則大樂與天地同其和。制爲彝倫〔之〕叙，〔立〕爲節，秩秩乎其有予也；流爲德澤，形爲〔歌〕頌，雍雍乎其有章也。于以定民志於無爲之際，而家〔家〕天下皆囿於吾禮之中，所謂「至禮不讓而天下治」者是已；于以和民心於不言之表，而家國天下舉歸於吾樂之內，所謂「至樂無聲〔而〕天下和」者是已。禮一制而民志以定，樂一〔奏〕而〔民〕心以和，刑措不
translation_en: … this. Allow me in my humble capacity to elaborate on this view: Heaven (which is also the same as humanity, having endowed him with matchless) virtue and also bestowed upon him the supreme (position—did it do so merely out of partiality for the sage, to honor) and glorify his person alone? Surely it was so that he might establish the mind for Heaven and Earth, establish destiny for the living people, and inaugurate great peace for ten thousand generations! When the sage emerges, replacing [?] Heaven in establishing the supreme standard and acting as parent to these people, how shall he look up and answer the intent behind High Heaven's endowment and bestowal? (Only) by establishing the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony in order to lead with rites and create music, and nothing more. Equilibrium and harmony are (the unmanifested rites and music within one's own person; rites and music are) the manifested equilibrium and harmony of one's own person. When in stillness there is no (partiality or inclination, then equilibrium reaches its utmost) equilibrium, and the great (foundation) is thereby established; when in movement there is not the slightest error or discrepancy, then harmony reaches its utmost harmony, and that is whereby the universal path operates. When the great foundation is established, the supreme standard of equilibrium is set up; when the universal path operates, the supreme standard of harmony is set up. Proceeding from this to lead with rites, the Great Rites share their regulation (with) Heaven and Earth; proceeding from this to create music, the Great Music shares its harmony with Heaven and Earth. Formulated into the order (of) the constant human relationships and (established) as regulations, how orderly and well-arranged they are [?]! Flowing forth as virtuous beneficence and taking form as (songs and) eulogies, how harmonious and resplendent they are! Thereby one settles the minds of the people in the realm of non-action, so that family after (family) [or: family, state,] and all under Heaven are encompassed within our rites—this is indeed what is meant by "supreme rites do not yield, yet all under Heaven is well-governed." Thereby one harmonizes the hearts of the people beyond spoken words, so that family, state, and all under Heaven are entirely brought within our music—this is indeed what is meant by "supreme music has no sound, (yet) all under Heaven is in harmony." Once rites are instituted, the minds of the people are settled; once music is (performed), the hearts of the (people) are harmonized. Punishments are set aside and not…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
用而兵革不試也萬國□□四夷來王也以
禮事上下而上下以諧樂和神祇而神祇以
和陰陽順序而海嶽受職也黎民於變而鳥獸
咸若也諸福之物可致之祥莫不畢至矣人心
附順沛乎若高屋而建瓴水也王業奠安屹乎
若南山而坐平原也非惟尊安於一日可以悠
久而無虞非徒尊安於一身以燕翼而不替
自一世□世百世猶一日也基統之垂
何遠哉自□世而至於千萬世千萬世猶一時
===
也基統之垂何邈哉禮樂之澤不泯則治道不
泯而基□□民焉禮樂之傳無窮則天慶無
窮而基業亦無窮焉商之中有震且業矣然
成湯置天下於禮樂之中其澤未泯也故高宗
撻然用武亦有以成中興之非垂萬世之基
而何歟周之鼎遷不絕如綫矣然文武周公制
作大備禮樂未息也故其衰弱之餘為天下之
共主者數十百年又非□萬世之基而何歟聖
人制禮作樂而垂統之意如此何莫不本於一
punctuated: 用，而兵革不試也；萬國□□，四夷來王也。以禮事上下，而上下以諧；樂和神祇，而神祇以和。陰陽順序，而海嶽受職也；黎民於變，而鳥獸咸若也。諸福之物，可致之祥，莫不畢至矣。人心附順，沛乎若高屋而建瓴水也；王業奠安，屹乎若南山而坐平原也。非惟尊安於一日，可以悠久而無虞；非徒尊安於一身，以燕翼而不替。自一世、□世、百世，猶一日也，基統之垂，何遠哉！自□世而至於千萬世，千萬世猶一時也，基統之垂，何邈哉！禮樂之澤不泯，則治道不泯，而基□□民焉；禮樂之傳無窮，則天慶無窮，而基業亦無窮焉。商之中，有震且業矣，然成湯置天下於禮樂之中，其澤未泯也，故高宗撻然用武，亦有以成中興之，非垂萬世之基而何歟？周之鼎遷，不絕如綫矣，然文、武、周公制作大備，禮樂未息也，故其衰弱之餘，為天下之共主者數十百年，又非□萬世之基而何歟？聖人制禮作樂，而垂統之意如此，何莫不本於一
translation_en: … unused, and weapons and armor are not put to the test; the myriad states […], and the four barbarian peoples come to pay homage to their sovereign. By serving those above and below with rites, those above and below are brought into harmony; by harmonizing the heavenly spirits and earthly deities with music, the heavenly spirits and earthly deities are brought into harmony. Yin and yang follow their proper sequence, and the seas and sacred peaks fulfill their offices; the black-haired people are transformed, and the birds and beasts are all compliant. All things of blessing and all attainable auspicious omens arrive in their entirety. The adherence and obedience of people's hearts are as torrential as pouring water from a pitcher on a high roof; the stability of the royal enterprise is as towering as the Southern Mountains sitting upon a level plain. Not only is one revered and secure for a single day, so that it may endure long without anxiety; not merely is one revered and secure in a single person, so as to shelter and give wing to posterity without decline. From one generation to […] generations and a hundred generations, it is as if a single day—how far-reaching is the handing down of the foundational lineage! From […] generations down to ten million generations, ten million generations are as if a single moment—how distant is the handing down of the foundational lineage! When the beneficence of rites and music does not perish, the way of governance does not perish, and the foundation […] [?]; when the transmission of rites and music is endless, the blessings of Heaven are endless, and the foundational enterprise is likewise endless. In the middle period of the Shang, there was shaking and peril; yet Cheng Tang 成湯 had placed the realm within rites and music, and their beneficence had not perished. Thus when Gaozong 高宗 briskly employed military force, he also had the means to achieve the [work] of restoration—what was this if not handing down a foundation for ten thousand generations? When the tripods of Zhou were moved, its line was as close to snapping as a thread; yet the institutions created by King Wen 文王, King Wu 武王, and the Duke of Zhou 周公 were grandly complete, and rites and music had not ceased. Thus, even in the aftermath of its decline and weakness, it remained the common sovereign of the realm for several hundred years—what again was this if not [handing down] a foundation for ten thousand generations? The sages' intention in instituting rites and creating music to hand down the lineage was such as this; how could it not be rooted in a single…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
身中和之極之建乎著之身以金樜玉之儀禮
之儀文似矣然而內多欲如中之極何作芝
房寶鼎之歌樂之節奏似矣然而外假仁義如
和之極何此武帝之雄才大畧雖足以致外觀
之美而中和之極未建不足以立萬世之基也
不覚言此可謂達禮樂之本矣其不能用也惜哉
是則中和之極建則禮樂不期於興而自興禮
樂之作其未不期於永而自永二帝三王
所以享國久久者用此道也漢唐宋之所以治
===
不古若者亦此道也洪惟我
朝
列聖建中和之極以衍慶於前我
聖上建中和之極以承休於後是以制作度越於
百王禮樂涵濡於四海垂萬世之基端在於
今日矣愚何幸躬逢其盛
表
擬宋歐陽脩辭侍讀學士表
牛奎宿
punctuated:
身中和之極之建乎？著之身以金樜玉之儀，禮之儀文似矣，然而內多欲，如中之極何？作芝房、寶鼎之歌，樂之節奏似矣，然而外假仁義，如和之極何？此武帝之雄才大畧，雖足以致外觀之美，而中和之極未建，不足以立萬世之基也。不覚言此，可謂達禮樂之本矣；其不能用也，惜哉！是則中和之極建，則禮樂不期於興而自興；禮樂之作，其未不期於永而自永。二帝、三王所以享國久久者，用此道也；漢、唐、宋之所以治不古若者，亦此道也。洪惟我朝列聖建中和之極以衍慶於前，我聖上建中和之極以承休於後，是以制作度越於百王，禮樂涵濡於四海，垂萬世之基，端在於今日矣。愚何幸躬逢其盛！

表

擬宋歐陽脩辭侍讀學士表

牛奎宿
translation_en:
…the establishment of the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony within one's own person? Displaying upon his person the ceremonies of golden mud and jade tablets [? 金樜玉], the outward forms of ritual seemed to be there; yet inwardly he was full of desires—what did this have to do with the ultimate standard of equilibrium? Composing the songs of the "Chamber of Auspicious Fungus" (Zhifang) and the "Precious Tripod" (Baoding), the rhythms of music seemed to be there; yet outwardly he merely feigned benevolence and righteousness—what did this have to do with the ultimate standard of harmony? Thus, although Emperor Wu of Han possessed heroic talent and grand strategy sufficient to achieve an impressive outward appearance, because the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony was not established, it was insufficient to lay a foundation for ten thousand generations. For Dong Zhongshu [? 不覚] to have spoken of this, he may truly be said to have grasped the fundamental basis of rites and music; that his words could not be put to use—how regrettable!

Therefore, when the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony is established, rites and music will flourish of themselves without our expecting them to flourish; and once rites and music are created, their legacy [? 其未] will endure of itself without our expecting it to endure. The reason the Two Emperors and Three Kings enjoyed such long-lasting reigns was that they employed this Way; the reason the governance of Han, Tang, and Song could not match antiquity was likewise because of this Way.

Humbly reflecting upon our dynasty: the successive sacred emperors established the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony to extend blessings in the past, and our Sacred Sovereign establishes the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony to inherit the glorious favor in the present. Therefore, our institutions far surpass those of the hundred kings, rites and music saturate the Four Seas, and the laying of a foundation for ten thousand generations truly rests in the present day. How fortunate am I to witness this flourishing era in person!

translation_en: …those serving as Readers-in-Waiting accounted for nearly half of them. Truly this was because he was a ruler of great accomplishment [?], a sovereign who examined antiquity and esteemed culture. As for Your Servant, I am a petty and lowly scholar, a mediocre talent like useless ailanthus and oak timber. Before my learning was fully formed, I suddenly rose to officialdom through the civil-service examinations; though my virtue does not match my rank, I still idly occupy a place in the court ranks. After awaiting punishment in the Hanlin Academy, I have been granted the post of Lecturer and Reader in the imperial講帷 (lecture tent). Although Your Majesty's sun-and-moon-like illumination does not overlook the obscure and mediocre, how can my ant-like, lowly body bear such a heavy burden? Surely there is no lack of renowned worthies in the world, and within the halls and pavilions of the Academy there are also many eminent elders. I beg that You take back the silken command of appointment, broadly seek out talents capable of ordering the state, and bestow this post upon such persons so that they may fill this position. Thus this pure office of careful selection will not be like a superfluous post received by routine, and worthies and men of ability [?] will advance together in categories, relieving Your Servant of anxiety [?]. Still, I hope that like the rising sun and arriving streams, Your Sacred Brilliance will advance ever further in illumination; and that lasting as long as Earth and Heaven, You will continue the unified enterprise for eternity. Your Servant is overcome to the utmost with looking up to Heaven and gazing upon Your Sacred Presence in earnest trepidation, and respectfully presents this memorial of declination and thanks to inform Your Majesty.

聖人作而繼天立極之功也，經作而扶世立教之道也。五之所在，道之所在也。前聖後聖，制作雖有不同，而扶世立教之心，亦曷嘗有不同哉？知乎此，則可以復明問之萬一矣，請申言之。天佑下民，作之君，作之師，以治之，以教之，無非欲納斯民於皇極也。稽之古，若舜之慎徽五典，此心此道也；禹之筆脩紀，此心此道也；武王之重民五教，庸非此心此道乎？是以當時學校興而教化明，人倫厚於下而風俗美，夫豈無自而然哉？洪惟我朝祖高皇帝，應人之庚此倫，乃以萬機之暇，條成

Policy Essays (ce)

First Question — Tian Kongzhao 田孔昭
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Wu 吳 comments: "This policy essay is able to recount in order the deeds and conduct of men of the past; he must be one who has devoted his mind to worldly moral instruction."
Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) You 游 comments: "Answered item by item without omission."
Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Hou 侯 comments: "Able to fulfill the intent of the question in his reply."

When the sages arose, theirs was the achievement of succeeding Heaven and establishing the supreme standard; when the classics [or canonical texts] were composed, theirs was the Way of sustaining the world and establishing moral instruction. Where the Five [Constant Relationships][?] reside is where the Way resides. Although the institutions created by former sages and later sages differed, how could their minds, bent on sustaining the world and establishing moral instruction, ever have differed? If one understands this, one may reply to one ten-thousandth of the enlightened question. Allow me to elaborate on this.

Heaven helps the people below, making for them rulers and making for them teachers to govern them and to instruct them, desiring nothing other than to bring these people into the August Ultimate (huangji). Examining antiquity: when Shun 舜 carefully beautified the Five Cardinal Duties (wudian), it was this mind and this Way; when Yu 禹 cultivated and ordered the human relationships (renji) [? 筆脩紀], it was this mind and this Way; when King Wu 武王 attached importance to the Five Teachings (wujiao) of the people, was this not also this mind and this Way? Therefore, at that time, schools flourished and moral transformation was made clear; human moral relationships were generous below and customs were admirable above[?]. Could this have come about without a source?

Humbly reflecting on our Dynasty: the Grand Progenitor (Taizu), Emperor Gao 高皇帝, fearing lest people transgress [? 應人之庚] these moral relationships, in his leisure from a myriad affairs of state compiled item by item…

宗文皇帝取人之道此倫〔乃於繼述之餘采古〕
人爲善行孝者作爲爲善陰隲孝順事實二書

人誦嘉惠臣民使之漸濡而目染其立教之心

===

孤則有〔五〕〔分〕令焉是皆爲善者也善者衆理
之會五倫豈外於此哉孝順實所載如忠孝
孝忠則有高登岳飛焉嚴寢廢詩則有蔡邕王
衣焉是皆行孝者也孝者百行之本五倫又豈

盡君臣之道者堯舜伊傅也能盡父子之道者
周公伯奇也盡夫婦之〔者非冀缺之與共姜〕

祈穀，孟夏雩于南郊，季秋大享于明堂，天寶以後有大清廟合祭於南。王仲丘、蕭嵩之所定議也，宜𠛬無所厎矣。然較之古者以大裘、袞冕以祭天，而祭地者有異，所以明天地之異用，昭郊社之□議者，又豈不失其宜乎？以至六天五帝之說，諸儒雖有不同之論，而朱子以爲一國三公如□，况有六天五帝乎？以□則六天五帝之謬爲可見。合祭之祭之說，詳儀雖有一□之議，而朱子以爲古者天地不合祭，日□□百神亦無一時共享之禮，由□□合祭之□爲可知。然郊以祭天于圜丘，明天道也；社以祭□方丘，明地道也。天地之道既明，則□本反治之禮無餘蘊矣。方今明御極，□古爲治，郊天祀地，藹然禮樂之明備，肅然誠敬之交乎，禮儀煥然，制度一新，有非區區漢、唐所能企及矣。愚也□何言哉？尚何言哉？

…to pray for grain, in the first month of summer performed the rain sacrifice (yu) in the southern suburbs, and in the last month of autumn held the Great Banquet (daxiang) in the Hall of Light (Mingtang); after the Tianbao era (742–756), there were the combined sacrifices at the Temple of Great Purity (Daqingmiao) in the south [?]. These were the rites deliberated and fixed by Wang Zhongqiu 王仲丘 and Xiao Song 蕭嵩, and it would seem nothing was amiss [?]. Yet when compared with the ancients, who wore the great fur robe (daqiu) and the ceremonial robe and crown (gunmian) to sacrifice to Heaven, while differing in those for sacrificing to Earth—whereby they clarified the different functions of Heaven and Earth and made manifest the […][?] discussions of the suburban and earth-altar sacrifices—how could they not also have lost what is proper? As for the theory of the Six Heavens and Five Emperors, although the various scholars held differing arguments, Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) considered that even having three dukes in a single state is like […], how much more so having Six Heavens and Five Emperors! From this […], the fallacy of the Six Heavens and Five Emperors can be seen. As for the theory of combined sacrifices [?], although those who detailed the ceremonies had arguments of a single […], Master Zhu held that in antiquity Heaven and Earth were not sacrificed to together, and that the sun, [moon, and] the hundred spirits likewise had no rite of sharing offerings at a single time; from [this,] the [fallacy] of combined sacrifices can be known. Indeed, the suburban sacrifice (jiao) offers sacrifice to Heaven at the Round Mound to illuminate the Way of Heaven; the altar of the soil (she) offers sacrifice to [Earth at] the Square Mound to illuminate the Way of Earth. Once the Ways of Heaven and Earth are illuminated, the rites of [repaying] the origin and returning to the beginning [?] leave nothing further unexpressed. Now, as our reigning sovereign occupies the throne and governs by [modeling on] antiquity, in sacrificing to Heaven in the suburbs and offering worship to Earth, how harmonious is the brilliant completeness of礼 and music, and how solemn is the mutual sincerity and reverence! The ceremonial rites are resplendent and the institutions wholly renewed, far beyond what the petty Han and Tang dynasties could ever hope to reach. What more could this foolish student say? What more could I possibly say?

… ministers like稷 [Ji, written 援] and Xie, they could not avoid relying on encouragement and exhortation [?], and thus the reputation of "incorruptible officials" first became prominent. He who feared the "four who know" and refused [gold] late at night—that was the outstanding purity of Yang Zhen 楊震. He who drank from the Spring of Greed yet grew ever fiercer in his resolve—that was the solitary integrity of Wu Yinzhi 吳隱之. Pacifying [蜀 Shu?] and returning east with nothing but maps and books—was that not [高] Rulun 高汝倫 [?]? Personally pacifying Jiangnan and loading his boats only with maps and registers—was that not [曹] Bin 曹彬? As for having no [?] estates and gardens, and as Chief Councilor being rich only in the Odes and Documents—this was the pure integrity of Fu Bi 富弼. Entering Shu with [a single cart?], accompanied only by a zither and a crane—this was the incorruptible scrupulousness of Zhao Bian 趙抃. [張] Jizhi 張及之 [or 李及 Li Ji?] not buying anything but [?] the collected works of Bai [Juyi], his [purity] can still be looked up to today; Bao Zheng 包拯 not [carrying away a single inkstone?], his lofty [?] demeanor can still be admired today.

Former Confucians said that in the reputation of incorruptible officials there are three kinds: First is natural [incorruptibility], such as the purity of Hu Zhi 胡質, who only feared that others would know of it. Second is affected [矯激, written 矯敖] incorruptibility, such as [Shouchun? 壽春 / 時苗 Shi Miao] leaving office and leaving behind the calf born there [?]. Third is forced [incorruptibility]—is that not someone who was once [?] extremely greedy and base, yet upon hearing the reputation of [董] Xuan 董宣 [or similar] changed his conduct?

Humbly I reflect that our Sacred [Emperor] reigns above, bringing about governance whose excellence surpasses Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] and rivals Yu and Zhou. Therefore, those who hold official [rank] possess the awe-inspiring pure integrity of the ancients, and those of wealth and noble rank display the admirable [靄靄, written 謁謁] lofty demeanor of the former worthies. All of them are naturally incorruptible and scrupulous, without affectation or forced effort. Those who enriched themselves only with the Odes and Documents or were accompanied only by a zither and a crane—although they are all worthy of emulation, if we ascend a step higher, in the end one must return to the same path as the sages and worthies [and nothing less]. [Your servant's] humble view is thus; [I] present it…

The methods of [military farming] across successive dynasties have differed, and the appropriateness of measures adapted to the times also has its basis. Since the military farms of antiquity each had their own [methods], when today we weigh the past to establish standards for the present, how could there not also be measures appropriate to the times? Understanding this, I may reply to the perceptive inquiry.

Now, when fields [are left uncultivated] and the state has military [campaigns], or when grain must be transported by canal and soldiers show the look of hunger, for anyone wishing to devise a plan to enrich the state and provision the army, what could [surpass] the method of military farms? Yet the ways in which military farms were established have each differed. When Emperor Wen (Wendi 文帝) recruited commoners to plough beneath the frontier defences, the idea of frontier agricultural colonies already existed; when Emperor Wu (Wudi 武帝) dispatched troops to farm at Dun煌 (Dunhuang 燉煌), the regulations for military farms took shape. When the Han opened communications with the Western Regions, it began with Commandants (Xiaowei 校尉) leading soldiers, so farming was carried out by troops; when the Tang established Military Prefectures (junfu 軍府) to set up agricultural colonies, the colonies were worked by civilians.
