translation_en:
… [who pushed the plan through and always] had stratagems, Cao Cao 曹操 (Duke Cao) was that man; during the Chunhua 淳化 era [?], Chen Shu 陳恕 (reading 亦矩 as 陳恕 [?]) proposed establishing state farms, and the Emperor's inclination leaned quite toward it, yet the one who obstructed that proposal was that man Huang Mao 黃懋. At present, the Dynasty examines antiquity to govern, and in the single matter of state farms (tuntian), it earnestly carries out the intention of benevolence and sympathetic solicitude within the articles of its laws and institutions. The common people submit to their transport of provisions, and the soldiers submit to their duties of warfare; there is nothing inconvenient for either soldiers or civilians, and nothing unsound in the institutions and laws.

The enlightened [examiner] also asks which dynasty should be taken as a model, and whose argument is appropriate. I, the ignorant one, beg to take the enduring and advantageous methods of the ancients, weigh what is practicable among them, and put them into practice without clinging stubbornly to [one corner?]; and as for the discussions of the ancients' good laws and fine intentions, consult and adopt what is worth adopting without being glued to narrowmindedness.

In antiquity, soldiers were lodged among the peasantry: in times of peace they were the people of the neighborhoods, villages, clans, and districts; in times of crisis they were the multitude of squads, companies, regiments, and ranks. […?] Later, those who served as soldiers engaged exclusively in military affairs, and those who governed them also no longer [treated them as farmers?]; thus soldiers were strictly soldiers, and civilians strictly civilians. If indeed on the frontier lands one uses soldiers for military farms and [in the interior?] uses civilians for civilian farms, holding the generals and commanders responsible for the soldiers and the Prefects and Magistrates responsible for the civilians, then although the [methods?] differ, in the end [reading 卞 as 下?] there will be nothing that does not succeed.

In antiquity, farming the frontier often supplied the expenses of the state; how could the frontier lands of today be impossible to farm? It is only that collective discussions are easily shaken and established laws remain unsettled: one says yes and another says no, that side approves and this side condemns. Hence there are those who raise the confounding argument that: "Just when spring farm work is at its height, frontier dust again sounds the alarm; just when the autumn grain is ripe, nomad horsemen again trample it." title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
地之可屯斷乎可行矣□也□□不足以博古才
不足以通今姑述其槩　對進而教之幸甚
第五問
李璽
考試官教〔諭游　批荅馭戎之道□□不為問目所窘其有用之學歟〕
考試官學正侯　批馭戎一策□□□用世之才足作評卷且有定□□他日嚮用必不□□矣科目得人如此寧不為之敬羨〕
呈□聞為高必因丘陵□□□必因川澤為政而不
===
□先王之道可謂智□馭戎而可以不法於
先王哉　先□□之馭戎□□以德以柔其暴義之
誠威以懲其不者之罪使□□威並施而已苟
或德之不脩威之不□又豈能使海宇寧謐華
夷一統哉□夫中國之有夷□猶晝之有夜陽
之有□自古不能無也有夏之時三苗負固不
服禹則誕敷文德舞干羽于兩階而七旬致其
來格焉是以德撫之□□□宣之時玁狁匪茹至
於涇陽宣王爰命吉甫□伐□至于大原而逐之
punctuated:
地之可屯，斷乎可行矣。□也□□不足以博古，才不足以通今，姑述其槩以對，進而教之，幸甚。

第五問

李璽

考試官教〔諭游批：荅馭戎之道，□□不為問目所窘，其有用之學歟！〕
考試官學正侯〔批：馭戎一策，□□□用世之才，足作評卷，且有定□□，他日嚮用，必不□□矣。科目得人如此，寧不為之敬羨！〕

呈□聞：為高必因丘陵，□□□必因川澤。為政而不□先王之道，可謂智□？馭戎而可以不法於先王哉？先□□之馭戎□□，以德以柔其慕義之誠，威以懲其不若之罪，使□□威並施而已。苟或德之不脩，威之不□，又豈能使海宇寧謐，華夷一統哉？□夫中國之有夷□，猶晝之有夜，陽之有□，自古不能無也。有夏之時，三苗負固不服，禹則誕敷文德，舞干羽于兩階，而七旬致其來格焉，是以德撫之□□。□宣之時，玁狁匪茹，至於涇陽，宣王爰命吉甫□伐□，至于大原而逐之…
translation_en:
…the borderlands can be farmed by military colonies is decidedly feasible. I, [name illegible], have [learning?] insufficient to be well-versed in antiquity, and talent insufficient to comprehend the present. I merely set forth the general outline in reply; if you advance me and instruct me, I shall be most fortunate.

Fifth Question

Li Xi 李璽

Examiner and Instructor You 游 [comments: In answering the way of controlling the western barbarians (Rong 戎), … he is not constrained by the points of the question. Is this not practical learning!]
Examiner and Director of Studies Hou 侯 [comments: This policy essay on controlling the western barbarians … talent useful to the world, sufficient to serve as a model evaluated paper [?], and moreover possesses definite [views/insight?]. When he is employed in the future, he will certainly not [disappoint?]. When the examination system obtains men like this, how can one not respect and admire it!]

I humbly [?] have heard: "To build high one must rely on hills and mounds; [to dig deep] one must rely on rivers and marshes." In governing, not to [follow] the way of the Former Kings—can that be called wise? And in controlling the western barbarians, how could one not model oneself upon the Former Kings? When the Former [Kings] controlled the barbarians, … they used virtue to mollify their sincerity in admiring righteousness [reading 暴 as 慕], and majesty to punish the crime of their recalcitrance [reading 不者 as 不若], simply causing [virtue and] majesty to be applied together. If virtue is not cultivated and majesty is not [established], how then could one bring peace and tranquility to the realm and unite Chinese and barbarians into one? Now, that the Central States have barbarian [peoples] is just as day has night and yang has [yin]; since antiquity it has been impossible for them not to exist. In the time of the Xia dynasty, the Three Miao (Sanmiao 三苗) relied on their strongholds and did not submit; Yu 禹 then grandly spread his civil virtue, dancing with shield and feather at the two staircases, and within seventy days brought them to come and submit—this was pacifying them with virtue …. In the time of King Xuan [of Zhou] (Zhou Xuanwang 周宣王), the Xianyun 玁狁 were recalcitrant and reached as far as Jingyang 涇陽; King Xuan thereupon commanded Jifu 吉甫 (Yin Jifu 尹吉甫) to [punish and] attack them, reaching as far as Taiyuan 大原 and driving them…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
遠邇焉是以威備之世　是以遠文德不脩威
武不振而夷狄之患始熾焉姑以西陲之務
通關陝者言之自夫平王東遷戎逼諸夏時至
春秋入洛戎強或入居於王城或來寇於京師
當是時也前有齊桓之徵諸侯後有晉文公之
會秦兵固嘗合師〔言以尊周室矣然私外假〕
仁義内濟其私豈能終格其〔心唐末以夷西〕
戎漸盛〔士謂求方務田作始畀以靈夏之地〕
終受其侵掠之後〔木以民也幸有狄青种世衡〕
===
之備邊韓琦范仲淹〔一下〕畧固嘗守邊備塞以
臣宋祚〔民西內治無〕〔亡政〕息豈能終致
其服乎況惟我
朝受天明命汛掃胡元文德之脩比隆乎虞周威
武之振超軼乎唐宋用是四夷率王蠻夷率服
所謂乎韓稽顙屠耆接踵者有不足言矣奈何
邇年以來西北虜酋肆其蜂蠆入我河套擾我
疆埸而士卒有征戍之　人民有轉輸之勞致
屢
punctuated: 遠邇焉，是以威備之世。是以遠文德不脩，威武不振，而夷狄之患始熾焉。姑以西陲之務通關陝者言之：自夫平王東遷，戎逼諸夏，時至春秋，入洛戎強，或入居於王城，或來寇於京師。當是時也，前有齊桓之徵諸侯，後有晉文公之會秦兵，固嘗合師〔言以尊周室矣，然私外假〕仁義，内濟其私，豈能終格其〔心？唐末以夷，西〕戎漸盛，〔士謂求方務田作，始畀以靈夏之地，〕終受其侵掠之後〔木以民也。幸有狄青、种世衡〕之備邊，韓琦、范仲淹〔一下〕畧，固嘗守邊備塞，以臣宋祚，〔民西內治無〕〔亡政〕息，豈能終致其服乎？況惟我朝受天明命，汛掃胡元，文德之脩比隆乎虞、周，威武之振超軼乎唐、宋，用是四夷率王，蠻夷率服，所謂乎韓稽顙、屠耆接踵者，有不足言矣。奈何邇年以來，西北虜酋肆其蜂蠆，入我河套，擾我疆埸，而士卒有征戍之，人民有轉輸之勞，致屢
translation_en:
… far and near; thus it was an age guarded by military awe. Later on [?], when civil virtue was not cultivated and military might was not roused, the menace of the non-Chinese tribes began to blaze forth. Let us speak for the moment of the affairs of the western frontier connected with Guanzhong and Shaanxi: ever since King Ping moved the capital east, the Rong tribes pressed upon the Chinese states. By the Spring and Autumn period, the Rong who entered the Luo River region grew strong, sometimes coming in to dwell in the royal capital, and sometimes coming to raid the metropolis. At that time, earlier there was Duke Huan of Qi summoning the feudal lords, and later there was Duke Wen of Jin meeting with the troops of Qin; they did indeed unite armies [claiming to honor the House of Zhou, yet outwardly borrowing the name of] benevolence and righteousness while inwardly serving their own selfish ends—how could they ultimately reform their [hearts? From the late Tang onward, the Western] Rong gradually grew powerful [… at first they were granted the lands of Lingzhou and Xiazhou [?],] and in the end the court suffered the aftermath of their invasions and plundering [… Fortunately during the Song there were Di Qing 狄青 and Chong Shiheng 种世衡] defending the frontier, and the strategic planning of Han Qi 韓琦 and Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹 […]. They did indeed guard the borders and prepare the frontier passes to uphold the imperial fortune of the Song [?], [yet domestically governance lacked …] rest [?], so how could they ultimately bring about their submission?

How much more so as Our Dynasty has received the bright mandate of Heaven and swept away the barbarian Yuan! The cultivation of our civil virtue matches the splendor of Yu [Shun] and the Zhou, and the rousing of our military might surpasses that of the Tang and the Song. Because of this, the tribes of the four quarters all acknowledge the sovereign and the southern and eastern barbarians all submit; such historical boasts as the Chanyu [?] knocking his head on the ground and the Tuqi kings following on one another's heels are not even worth mentioning! Why is it, then, that in recent years the caitiff chieftains of the northwest have given free rein to their wasp-and-scorpion venom, entering our Ordos Loop (Hetao) and harassing our borderlands, so that our soldiers suffer the hardships of campaign and garrison duty, and our people bear the toil of transporting supplies, repeatedly causing…

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
守軫念西陲命將出師撃〔之致討殲厥渠魁大獻〕
俘捷狼藉餘孽望風遠〔遁矣然誠太平無疆之〕
休也第恐醜虜窮恙復懷覬覦令日豫為猶謀
莫如二三將練兵以待之則彼犬羊知我有備必
不敢再犯我邊庭矣萬一肆〔其效尤必須出奇〕
制勝以撃之則彼狐〔鼠〕畏威遠遁必不敢竊入
我疆土矣雖然司惟其中有故其後變乃出
不備之〔策〕其窮兵〔古〕單于入自其所置
之郡是皆失其馭之〔之〕道也方今
===
聖人在上德並春生威同〔秋〕殺居左右者皆皐夔之
儔守邊〔之〕韓范之〔也〕叙戎之術一法古人
德以來其慕義之誠威以禦〔其〕不恭之罪〔簒〕
小虜將格心而自附〔矣〕又何邊患之足慮哉〔管〕
見如斯未知可否惟執事進〔而〕之
punctuated: 守軫念西陲，命將出師，撃〔之致討，殲厥渠魁，大獻〕俘捷，狼藉餘孽，望風遠〔遁矣。然誠太平無疆之〕休也。第恐醜虜窮恙，復懷覬覦，令日豫為猶謀，莫如二三將練兵以待之，則彼犬羊知我有備，必不敢再犯我邊庭矣；萬一肆〔其效尤，必須出奇〕制勝以撃之，則彼狐〔鼠〕畏威遠遁，必不敢竊入我疆土矣。雖然，司惟其中有故，其後變乃出不備之〔策〕，其窮兵〔古〕單于入自其所置之郡，是皆失其馭之〔之〕道也。方今聖人在上，德並春生，威同〔秋〕殺，居左右者皆皐、夔之儔，守邊〔之〕韓、范之〔也〕，叙戎之術，一法古人，德以來其慕義之誠，威以禦〔其〕不恭之罪，〔簒〕小虜將格心而自附〔矣〕，又何邊患之足慮哉？〔管〕見如斯，未知可否，惟執事進〔而〕之。
translation_en:
…the Sovereign [? 守 for 皇上] has been deeply concerned about the western frontier, ordering generals to lead out campaigns to strike them and exact punishment, annihilating their ringleaders and presenting great captives and victories, while the scattered remnants fled afar at the mere wind of our advance. Truly this is the boundless blessing of great peace! Yet I fear that the vile caitiffs in their desperate distress [? 窮恙] may once again harbor covetous designs. In taking advance counsel today, nothing is better than selecting generals and drilling troops to await them; then those dogs and sheep, knowing that we are prepared, will surely not dare to invade our frontier courts again. Should one in ten thousand indulge in following their bad example, we must employ surprise tactics to win victory and strike them; then those foxes and rats, awed by our majesty and fleeing afar, will surely not dare to steal into our territory.

Even so, [? 司惟其中有故] when later crises arose out of unpreparedness [?], or when through the exhaustion of military force [?], as in antiquity when the Chanyu entered through the commanderies that had been established for them—all of these lost the proper way of controlling them. At present, a Sage is on the throne, his virtue matching the life-giving force of spring and his majesty like the withering frost of autumn; those who attend him on the left and right are all the equals of Gao Yao 皐陶 and Kui 夔, and those who guard the frontiers are the likes of Han Qi 韓琦 and Fan Zhong淹 范仲淹. In the art of managing the western barbarians [? 叙戎 for 馭戎], we wholly model ourselves on the ancients: using virtue to attract their sincere admiration for righteousness, and using majesty to ward off the crime of their disrespect. The petty caitiffs [? 簒 for 蠢] will reform their hearts and submit of their own accord; what frontier troubles would then be worth worrying about? Such is my humble view; not knowing whether it is acceptable or not, I pray only that Your Excellency bring it forward and [instruct me?].

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陝西鄉試錄後序
人君代天理物莫先於求賢而求
賢莫先於科目焉夫是蓋以豪傑
之士肯由此焉出非科目不足以得
人也欲求真才舍科目奚以哉洪
惟
===
列聖相承養士以興設取士以科目良
以□□百餘年□□咸寧四夷
來王豈非得人而致之歟其間奠
安宗社足以匹伊保乂王家
足以媲美韓范者肩摩踵接詩所
謂濟濟多士文王以寧書所謂九
德咸事俊乂在官是已猗歟盛哉
punctuated:
陝西鄉試錄後序

人君代天理物，莫先於求賢；而求賢莫先於科目焉。夫是，蓋以豪傑之士肯由此焉出，非科目不足以得人也。欲求真才，舍科目奚以哉？洪惟列聖相承，養士以興設，取士以科目。良以□□，百餘年□□咸寧，四夷來王，豈非得人而致之歟？其間奠安宗社，足以匹伊；保乂王家，足以媲美韓、范者，肩摩踵接。《詩》所謂「濟濟多士，文王以寧」，《書》所謂「九德咸事，俊乂在官」，是已。猗歟盛哉！
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

When a ruler governs all things on behalf of Heaven, nothing takes precedence over seeking the worthy; and in seeking the worthy, nothing takes precedence over the civil service examination system. Indeed, this is because outstanding scholars are willing to emerge by this path [?], and without the examination system it would be impossible to obtain capable men. If one wishes to seek true talent, how could it be done while setting aside the examinations?

Reflecting broadly upon how the successive sacred emperors have carried on the heritage one after another, they have nurtured scholars through established institutions [?] and selected scholars through the examination system. Truly because of […], for over a hundred years [all within the empire?] has enjoyed complete peace, and the four barbarians have come to pay homage as subjects—was this not brought about by obtaining capable men? During this time, those who stabilized the ancestral altars and state altars—sufficient to match Yi Yin (伊尹) [and Zhou Gong?]—and those who protected and governed the royal house—sufficient to rival the glory of Han Qi (韓琦) and Fan Zhongyan (范仲淹)—have stood shoulder to shoulder and followed closely on one another's heels. What the Book of Odes (Shijing) calls "Thickly gather the many officers, and through them King Wen enjoys repose," and what the Book of Documents (Shujing) calls "When men of the nine virtues all serve, the eminent and able are in office"—this is truly it! How magnificent and flourishing indeed!

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
成化甲午歲當〔大〕比陝西藩臬重
臣先期謀于巡〔按〕左副都御史馬
文升巡按監察御史王錡走禮幣
聘邦貞等爲考試官旣期畢集于
時監察御史王錦繼任其事而總
理〔之〕晝夜〔之〕勤〔勤〕□白一心期
得眞才以副
===
試典合八郡三邊〔之〕士一千有奇循
例〔試〕者〔試〕者〔試〕其言之純乎
理者取之如額錄成□謂邦貞宜
序諸後予惟諸士子〔之〕逢
聖明亨嘉之運際此雲龍風虎之會誠
千載奇遇也〔得〕〔與〕其名禮闈進對
大廷顯融有日矣公〔且〕夫
punctuated: 成化甲午，歲當〔大〕比，陝西藩臬重臣先期謀于巡〔按〕左副都御史馬文升、巡按監察御史王錡，走禮幣聘邦貞等爲考試官。旣期畢集，于時監察御史王錦繼任其事，而總理〔之〕，晝夜〔之〕勤〔勤〕，□白一心，期得眞才以副試典。合八郡三邊〔之〕士一千有奇，循例〔試〕者〔試〕者，〔試〕其言之純乎理者，取之如額。錄成，□謂邦貞宜序諸後。予惟諸士子〔之〕逢聖明亨嘉之運，際此雲龍風虎之會，誠千載奇遇也。〔得〕〔與〕其名，禮闈進對大廷，顯融有日矣。公〔且〕夫…
translation_en: In the jiawu year of the Chenghua era (1474), the year of the triennial Provincial Examination, the senior officials of the Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commission and Surveillance Commission consulted in advance with Grand Coordinator [巡撫, OCR: 巡〔按〕] and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Ma Wensheng 馬文升 and Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor Wang Qi 王錡, and dispatched ritual gifts to invite me, Bangzhen 邦貞, and others to serve as Examiners. When the appointed time arrived and everyone had assembled, Investigating Censor Wang Jin 王錦 succeeded to the post and assumed overall management of the affair. Toiling tirelessly day and night, pure [□白] and united in heart, they hoped to obtain true talent to fulfill the examination statutes. Bringing together more than one thousand scholars from the eight prefectures and three frontier regions, they tested them in three sessions according to precedent [循例〔試〕者〔試〕者, 〔試〕?], and selected up to the prescribed quota those whose words were pure in principle. When the examination record was completed, [they] said that I, Bangzhen, ought to write a postface at the end. I reflect that for the scholars to encounter the prosperous fortune of a sage and enlightened reign, and to meet with this gathering of clouds and dragons, wind and tigers, is truly a rare encounter of a thousand years. Having placed their names on this roster, the day when they will advance through the Metropolitan Examination at the Ministry of Rites to reply at the Great Court and achieve illustrious eminence is close at hand. [? 公] Moreover, …

title: 成化十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
朝廷之御我也設之學校立之師傅
豐其廩餼教養之心至矣盡矣
恩莫大焉主司之選我也鑑空衡平
妍媸自見錙銖不爽矣選之心精
矣密矣公莫過焉與斯選也何其
榮榮哉　茲以之有祿位要
必爲上不負爲下爲民不忝舜吾
君不忝辟吾民所忠也不伊周德
業之聊資事功也始爲此心
終爲此心獨成治化比隆於前代
===
追配於古人庶無負
王明教養之恩無負主司選舉之公無
負己之所學所志矣苟或言與行
違志與道違終之始遠則非予輩
punctuated: 朝廷之御我也，設之學校，立之師傅，豐其廩餼，教養之心至矣、盡矣，恩莫大焉；主司之選我也，鑑空衡平，妍媸自見，錙銖不爽矣，選之心精矣、密矣，公莫過焉。與斯選也，何其榮榮哉！茲以之有祿位，要必爲上不負，爲下爲民不忝，舜吾君、不忝辟吾民，所忠也；不伊、周德業之聊，資事功也。始爲此心，終爲此心，獨成治化，比隆於前代，追配於古人，庶無負王明教養之恩，無負主司選舉之公，無負己之所學、所志矣。苟或言與行違，志與道違，終之始遠，則非予輩
translation_en: … In the Imperial Court's governing of us, it establishes schools for us, appoints teachers and tutors for us, and generously provides grain stipends; its intention in educating and nurturing us reaches the utmost and leaves nothing undone—no grace could be greater than this. In the examiners' selection of us, the mirror is clear and the balance level, so that beauty and ugliness reveal themselves of their own accord and not a fraction of a grain is amiss; their intention in selecting [?us] is refined and meticulous—no impartiality could surpass this. To be included in this selection—how glorious it is! Now, proceeding from this to hold emoluments and official rank, you must above all not fail your superiors above, and below not bring shame upon the people; making our sovereign a Shun and not shaming the governance [?] of our people is where your loyalty lies, and not resting content [?] before achieving the moral accomplishments of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou is what contributes to your practical achievements [?]. Hold to this mind from the beginning, and hold to this mind to the end, so as to accomplish transformative governance that rivals the splendor of former eras and matches the ancients. Thus you may perhaps not fail the grace of the enlightened sovereign's education and nurture, not fail the impartiality of the examiners' selection, and not fail your own learning and aspirations. Should your words go against your deeds, your aspirations go against the Way, and your end diverge far from your beginning, then that is not what I and my colleagues …
